title: Self-hosting is the differentiator that beats six of the eight commercial peers, it is asserted in six separate marketing surfaces, and AUDIT-014#host-01 proves it does not currently work
category: competitive positioning: list (b), the load-bearing advantage
description: Of the eight commercial DAST vendors researched (Detectify, Intruder, Probely/Snyk, Pentest-Tools.com, Acunetix/Invicti, Burp Suite DAST, Snyk, Astra), only Burp Suite DAST and Acunetix/Invicti offer real self-hosting; the other six are SaaS with at most an internal-scanning agent (audits/AUDIT-014/research-competitors-commercial.md, "Deployment" section). GPL-3.0 plus a working self-host is therefore the single structural advantage that no amount of engineering by a small team could otherwise buy. The product asserts it in six places: components/landing/landing-open-source.tsx:39 ("Self-hosting is one Dockerfile and a Postgres connection string"), app/landing/page.tsx:82 (FAQ: "Yes. The whole thing is GPL-3.0 and runs on your own infrastructure"), app/landing/page.tsx:57 (the definitional FAQ answer), components/landing/landing-use-cases.tsx:21 ("a self-host path if the SaaS is a non-starter"), lib/seo/alternatives.ts:46 (the shared VR.hosting string reused on all five /alternatives pages), and lib/seo/alternatives.ts:103, :250, :317 (per-competitor FAQ answers repeating it). AUDIT-014#host-01 (critical) found that on an empty database instrumentation.ts exits 1 before creating a single table, and AUDIT-014#host-02 found the Dockerfile runtime stage never copies scripts/, so db:create and db:migrate are unrunnable inside the published image. Merged from mkt-03, which filed the same fact from the marketing surface. Its point stands and is folded in here: the recommendation is to keep the self-hosting copy rather than weaken it, because the marketing surface is itself the argument for prioritising the host-01 and host-02 fixes. If they cannot be fixed quickly, the copy has to change instead, since it is currently false on the landing page and in the README.
impact: Every competitive claim on the site rests on a capability that a new self-hoster cannot currently exercise. A developer who reaches /alternatives/detectify, reads "self-host it yourself with no plan limits", clones the repo and fails at first boot does not file a bug: they conclude the open-source claim is decorative and leave. This is the one advantage the eight commercial peers structurally cannot copy, and it is the one that does not work.
recommendation: Treat AUDIT-014#host-01 and #host-02 as competitive-blocking, not just deploy bugs: fix them before any further marketing or SEO work in section 19. Then add a CI job that runs the documented self-host path end to end (fresh Postgres container, docker compose up, assert /api/v3/health returns healthy) so the claim cannot silently rot again. Only once that job is green, promote self-hosting from a paragraph in components/landing/landing-open-source.tsx to a named comparison row in lib/seo/alternatives.ts's shared VR object, phrased against the verified fact: "Self-host it. Six of the eight commercial web scanners cannot be run on your own infrastructure at any price."

title: Four marketing surfaces claim scans finish in under 3 seconds while the shipped scan path still awaits a 15s subdomain discovery, so the visitor watches the claim fail on the first scan
description: The under-3-seconds claim is published in five places: app/landing/page.tsx:31 (the page meta description, "get a security report in under 3 seconds"), app/landing/page.tsx:77 (the FAQ answer "Under 3 seconds for a standard scan", which is also emitted as FAQPage structured data via FaqStructuredData at :110), components/landing/landing-hero.tsx:61 (the stat strip entry ["<3s", "per scan"]), components/landing/landing-how-it-works.tsx:46 ("Most scans are done in under three seconds"), and README.md:8. components/landing/landing-api-example.tsx:23 also ships a sample response with "duration": 2841. AUDIT-011#scan-01 established the engine does not meet that on the signed-in path, and the cause is still present: lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:791-795 still awaits autoSubdomainsPromise, capped at 15000ms by lib/scanner/subdomain-auto.ts, and components/scanner/scanning-indicator.tsx:118 still starts the client stopwatch that AUDIT-011#scan-05 measured at 15 to 20 seconds. Verified at those exact lines in the current tree. The only surface where the claim holds is the demo, and only because app/api/v3/demo-scan/route.ts skips subdomain discovery entirely, which means the visitor sees 3 seconds in the demo and 17 seconds on their first real scan.
impact: The product's headline differentiator is contradicted by the product roughly thirty seconds after the visitor reads it, on the first scan they run as a signed-up user. A specific number that turns out to be wrong by 5x is worse than no number, because it teaches the reader that the rest of the page's very specific claims (stable IDs, deterministic severities, real evidence) may be equally decorative. The FAQ answer is also syndicated as FAQPage structured data, so the false number is what an answer engine quotes.
recommendation: Fix the engine, do not soften the copy: AUDIT-011#scan-01 specifies a roughly 10-line change at lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:791-802 and lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:698 that makes every one of these five claims true again. If that will not ship this cycle, remove the number rather than publish a false one. Interim copy: app/landing/page.tsx:31 becomes "Paste a URL and get ${TOTAL_CHECKS_LABEL} deterministic checks back across headers, TLS, cookies, DNS, and secrets. Same URL, same finding IDs, every run. No agent to install." app/landing/page.tsx:75-78 FAQ becomes question "How long does a scan take?" answer "Checks run in parallel rather than in sequence, and the report shows the exact duration for your target. Slow DNS or a long certificate chain is what moves the number." components/landing/landing-hero.tsx:58-63 drops the speed stat and becomes [[checkCount, "checks"], [categoryCount, "categories"], ["0", "models in the detection path"], ["GPL-3.0", "licensed"]], which keeps the mono tabular-nums idiom and swaps the one number the product cannot back for the one differentiator it can. components/landing/landing-how-it-works.tsx:45-49 becomes "Everything runs in parallel, so the wall clock is the slowest module, not the sum of them. The report tells you exactly how long yours took."

title: The root layout awaits headers() for a CSP nonce, so all 311 routes render per-request and every one of the ~790 public pages is served private, no-cache, no-store
description: app/layout.tsx:146 does `const nonce = (await headers()).get("x-nonce")` to feed the nonce on the inline auth-cache <script> at app/layout.tsx:158. Reading headers() in the root layout opts every segment beneath it into per-request dynamic rendering. The committed build proves it: .next/prerender-manifest.json lists exactly 5 prerendered routes (/robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, /manifest.webmanifest, /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt) and 0 dynamicRoutes, against 311 entries in .next/app-build-manifest.json. app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:34 still runs generateStaticParams() over all ~754 checks at build time and produces nothing; its own comment at line 29 acknowledges this ('The root layout reads headers() for its CSP nonce, so the whole app already renders per-request'). Next.js sets `cache-control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate` on dynamically-rendered app pages (node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/cache-control.js:15), and nothing in middleware.ts or next.config.mjs overrides it -- grepping Cache-Control across middleware.ts and lib/ returns one unrelated hit in lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts:142. So /checks/*, /checks/category/*, /alternatives/*, /docs/*, /changelog, /pricing, /compare and /landing are all re-rendered from scratch on every single request and are uncacheable by the browser, by Cloudflare, and by any CDN in front of the app.
impact: The entire SEO surface, which is the product's growth engine (~754 /checks pages plus category, docs, alternatives and compare pages), pays a full origin React render on every crawler hit and every visitor, with zero edge caching. A search-engine crawl of the check index is ~790 cold SSRs against one Node process that is also running scans. TTFB for anonymous marketing traffic is pinned to origin latency rather than the CDN, and traffic spikes hit the origin directly instead of being absorbed by Cloudflare.
recommendation: Drop the nonce. The inline script at app/layout.tsx:158 is build-time constant (its only interpolation is JSON.stringify over STAFF_ROLES), so compute its sha256 at build and put 'sha256-...' in the script-src of middleware.ts instead of 'nonce-...'; then delete the `await headers()` at app/layout.tsx:146 and the nonce prop. With the layout static, add `export const revalidate` to app/checks/[id]/page.tsx, app/checks/category/[category]/page.tsx, app/alternatives/[competitor]/page.tsx and the docs pages so generateStaticParams actually produces ISR-cached HTML. If the nonce must stay, move the nonce-consuming script into a route-group layout that only wraps the authenticated app (/dashboard, /history, /profile, /admin, ...) and leave the public marketing/SEO group on a static layout.

title: Five real OAuth error codes render an empty string, so a failed Discord sign-in shows a normal login form
description: The ?error= mapper at app/login/page.tsx:47-89 has no catch-all and ends in `return ""`. Five codes the OAuth callback actually emits are unmapped: discord_invalid, discord_not_configured, discord_invalid_state, discord_user_failed, session_expired.
impact: A Discord sign-in that fails for any of these reasons bounces the user back to a login form that looks completely normal, with no message at all. They retry and fail identically, with no path to understanding why.
recommendation: Add a catch-all before `return ""`, for example 'Sign-in failed. Try again, or use another method.'

title: The findings bulk-remediation toolbar is the only true bulk action in the product, and it is poor enough to justify removal
description: Select mode lives at components/scanner/results-list.tsx:122-226 with the toggle at :440-458, the row checkbox at :659-669 and the bulk bar at :685-770. It is gated by scanUrl from canRemediate (components/scanner/scan-result-detail.tsx:71-74) so it appears only on /dashboard after a scan and on /history?id=n. Four specific problems: (1) in select mode the row body is still a full-width button that navigates (:811-813), and opening a finding unmounts ResultsList entirely (its own comment at :228-234 says so) while selected, selectMode and overlay are all local useState, so one mis-tap on row 38 of 200 wipes the selection with no persistence anywhere; (2) selection ignores filters silently, so narrowing the severity filter leaves hidden picks selected and Apply hits findings the user cannot see; (3) at 360px the bar wraps to three rows, roughly 130-160px, a quarter of the viewport, pinned over the list being selected from, one of those rows being a cramped native date picker; (4) the backend is a bulk endpoint in name only, fanning out to Promise.all of up to 200 independent pool.query calls with no transaction (app/api/v3/scan/remediation/bulk/route.ts:83-119), so partial failure leaves partial state behind a generic 'Couldn't apply. Try again.' There is no select-all, no per-group select, no shift-click range, no keyboard toggle (shiftKey appears nowhere in the repo), no confirmation and no undo, and status 'open' deletes each row including notes and assignees irreversibly.
impact: The one place multi-select carries real weight, triaging the 100+ findings a crawl scan produces, is the place it works worst. Users lose selections to mis-taps and cannot tell which findings an Apply actually touched.
recommendation: Owner's call, and both paths are costed. REMOVE is roughly 565 lines: results-list.tsx ~235 (893 to ~660), the route 128, its tests 111, openapi-spec.ts ~35, docs/triage ~40, docs-knowledge.md ~15, plus one line each in client-constants.ts:226, scan-result-detail.tsx, dashboard-results.tsx:232 and history/page.tsx:499. useTeammates survives (issue-detail.tsx:296 also uses it) and the per-finding RemediationControl remains as the fallback. REDESIGN is roughly two days: delete the mode toggle and make the row's left severity bar a 36px selection target; lift selection into lib/hooks/use-finding-selection.ts backed by sessionStorage keyed on scanUrl so it survives navigation; add tri-state select-all on the count line and on each severity group header; collapse the toolbar to '[N selected] [Mark as v] [Clear]' on desktop and a full-width action sheet of five 44px rows on mobile; add x to toggle, shift-click to extend, Esc to clear; replace confirmation with an 8-second Undo, which requires capturing prior remediation rows and giving the route an items[] body shape; and replace the Promise.all fan-out with one INSERT ... SELECT ... FROM unnest(...) inside a transaction so the all-or-nothing error copy becomes honest.

title: The monthly to yearly upgrade has no entry point because the current-plan check ignores billing interval
description: components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:124 is `const isCurrentPlan = currentPlan === plan.id;`, which ignores the billing interval. Flipping the hero's -20% monthly/yearly toggle still renders a disabled 'Current Plan' button for a user on the monthly tier.
impact: /checkout/pro_supporter_yearly is reachable only by typing the URL, even though app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:199 already ships 'Switch to yearly billing' copy for it. The 20 percent annual upsell has no entry point anywhere in the product.
recommendation: Compare the billing interval as well as the plan id.

title: 'Go to the dashboard now' does not navigate, stranding the user on a success screen during a slow confirmation
description: components/billing/stripe-checkout.tsx:121 calls onSuccess(), which renders the 'You are subscribed' screen while confirmation is still retrying, and never navigates anywhere. The three credit components use a real <Link>.
impact: The user clicks the escape hatch during a slow confirmation and is left on a success screen for a subscription that may not have confirmed.
recommendation: Use <Link href={ROUTES.DASHBOARD}> as the three sibling components do.

title: /compare fails silently and permanently on every error, with an explicitly no-op catch
description: app/compare/page.tsx:54-64 fetches the compare endpoint, sets diffResult only `if (res.ok)`, has no else branch, and catches with `/* ignore */`. A 403 (a shared link to someone else's scans), a 404 (deleted scan), a 500 or a dropped connection all land identically: loading flips false, diffResult stays null, and the UI re-renders the scan picker with the Compare button live again. app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:238-240 already has the correct pattern in-repo.
impact: The user clicks Compare, watches a spinner, and is returned exactly where they started with no explanation. Clicking again reproduces it forever. A shared /compare link the recipient cannot access shows the generic host picker with no hint why.
recommendation: Add an error state set in both the non-ok branch and the catch, rendered above the Compare button.

title: POST /api/v3/scan/bulk is fully built and has no UI caller; the dashboard loops single scans instead
description: app/api/v3/scan/bulk/route.ts is 734 lines and accepts {urls[], isPublic}, scanning up to a plan-capped 100 URLs in one request. API.SCAN_BULK is declared at lib/config/constants.ts:747 and referenced by nothing outside the docs pages and landing-api-example.tsx:118. The dashboard's bulk panel instead loops POST /api/v3/scan one URL at a time at app/dashboard/page.tsx:743-775, and detects rate limits by string-matching error text at :762-763. The two paths have separately-audited quota and privacy handling. Note also that FEATURE_BULK_SCANS gates only the unused public endpoint (scan/bulk/route.ts:346), so disabling the flag does not disable the dashboard's bulk tab.
impact: The first-party UI pays N round trips for what the server does in one, repeatedly trips its own burst limiter, reports failure per URL instead of atomically, and diverges from the audited code path. Bulk scanning is a sold plan feature priced 5/10/25/100 across tiers.
recommendation: Point handleBulkScan at API.SCAN_BULK with the whole array. Roughly 40 lines out of app/dashboard/page.tsx replaced by about 15, and the feature flag starts working.

title: Plan limits displayed to users come from a hardcoded catalog while enforcement reads 48 admin-editable settings
description: components/pricing/pricing-features.tsx:186-187 carries the comment 'These numbers come straight out of the billing config, so this table cannot drift from what the API actually enforces', but it reads PLANS[].limits from lib/billing/catalog.ts:115-233, a hardcoded copy. Enforcement reads the 48 BILLING_* registry settings via lib/billing/plan-limits.ts:19-82. The same hardcoded read occurs at components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:157, components/modals/premium-upgrade-modal.tsx:79/89, app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:204,223,294, components/profile/tabs/profile-billing-tab.tsx:1493 and app/pricing/page.tsx:28-36. It is done correctly at app/api/v3/billing/route.ts:82-94 and app/api/v3/auth/me/route.ts:111,184, which resolve live.
impact: Values match today so there is no present drift, but any one of 48 admin edits silently desynchronises what is advertised from what is enforced, on the pricing page, in the upgrade modal and on the checkout page. The comment asserting this cannot happen makes it less likely anyone checks.
recommendation: Have the display surfaces resolve limits live the way app/api/v3/billing/route.ts:82-94 does, and delete the comment at pricing-features.tsx:186-187.

title: The scanning page timer undersells the engine and should be removed once the latency is fixed
description: components/scanner/scanning-indicator.tsx:118 starts a pure client stopwatch with useState(() => Date.now()), ticked at :149 and rendered at :271-273. It starts at setStatus('scanning') in app/dashboard/page.tsx:471, before the POST at :537, and stops only when React unmounts the indicator at :910. It floors the value (:77-81), so a displayed '17s' means at least 17.0 real seconds. Separately, the server-reported 'Scan duration' stat (components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:303-310, from result.duration, snapshotted at lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:823) also includes the subdomain wait since commit 3a242f89. Both numbers are honest and both show roughly 17s. The 2-5s engine time is not surfaced anywhere in the product. Verified NOT the cause: there is no artificial minimum display time (the cosmetic timers at :42, :58, :69 cannot hold the flip because the component is unmounted by the status conditional), no serial post-completion fetches, and no router.refresh().
impact: The product's core differentiator is speed, and the only number the user watches contradicts it on every scan.
recommendation: Fix scan-01 first. Then replace the elapsed-seconds readout with progress that carries information rather than a number that invites comparison: the check family currently running, the count of checks completed against the total, and the findings counter ticking up as they land. If a duration is shown at all after the fix, show the server-reported engine time and label it as such.

title: The AI chat launcher covers the Save Changes button on /profile and the bottom-right of every commerce form
description: components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:1613-1617 renders a 56px FAB at bottom-5 right-5 z-50, mounted after children. Its route gating at :1273-1284 returns null on /browser/, /docs and /admin, but not /profile. At 375px the save card spans to right:16px with right-aligned buttons, so the FAB occupying right 20-76px and y 20-76px sits directly over Save Changes.
impact: Compounds shell-02 on /profile: even after dismissing the cookie notice, the chat launcher still covers the save button on a phone. Also covers the bottom-right of forms on /pricing, /checkout, /contact, /legal and the auth pages.
recommendation: Offset the launcher by --vr-cookie-h and give the floating save bars right padding that clears 76px on mobile, or add /profile to the launcher's null-return route list.

title: The teammate scan 'View' button links to a hash the history page never reads, using the wrong id
description: components/teams/team-member-scans.tsx:107 renders `<a href={`/history#${scan.id}`}>`. /history reads only ?scan=<public_id> (app/history/page.tsx:161,176-178) and nothing anywhere reads location.hash. Compounding this, MemberScan.id is the numeric primary key (components/teams/teams-types.ts:47), not the opaque public_id the route resolves.
impact: Clicking View drops the user on the unfiltered history list with no indication of what happened. Both halves are wrong, so even adding hash handling would not fix it.
recommendation: Return public_id from /api/v3/teams/member-scans and link to `/history?scan=${scan.publicId}`.

title: Teammate scan panel can display one member's scans under another member's name
description: app/teams/page.tsx:459-481 sets viewingMember unconditionally at :464 and only assigns memberScans inside the `if (res.ok)` branch at :472. memberScans is never cleared. After a successful load for member A, a failed load for member B leaves A's scan list in state while the heading renders `{member.name}'s Scan History` (components/teams/team-member-scans.tsx:45). The memberScansReqRef ticket guards response ordering but not the error path, which is the same class of mislabel it was written to prevent.
impact: One teammate's scanned URLs are displayed under a different teammate's name. On a team feature this is a trust and privacy problem, not just a rendering bug.
recommendation: Call setMemberScans([]) before the fetch and add an explicit error branch that renders a failure state rather than leaving stale data on screen.

title: The AI chat textarea, the support-ticket reply box and four other user-facing inputs have only a placeholder, no accessible name
description: A scan of all 144 Input/Textarea/input/textarea/select elements in app/, components/ and lib/ found these with no id + htmlFor pair, no aria-label and no wrapping <label>: components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:1541 (the AI assistant's message box, mounted on every page via ChatWidget in app/layout.tsx:190); components/contact/support-tickets.tsx:609 (the reply box on a support ticket, available on every tier); components/history/history-notes.tsx:82 (scan notes); components/teams/team-detail-header.tsx:79 (rename a team); app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:406 (request-body textarea, the sibling of AUDIT-011#docs-07's :514 which cited only the param inputs); components/admin/features/support-inbox.tsx:344 (staff reply). Each has a `placeholder` only, and a placeholder is not an accessible name: it is not exposed as the field's name by the accname algorithm when it is the sole source in several screen-reader/browser pairings, and it disappears the moment the user types. This is the same defect AUDIT-011#docs-07 filed against the playground, present on the general product surface rather than in docs. app/legal/accessibility/page.tsx:88-91 publishes "Form Labels: All form inputs have associated labels for clarity."
impact: A screen-reader user who tabs into the AI support widget hears "edit, blank" with no indication of what the field is for, and the same on a support-ticket reply. Voice-control users cannot say "click <field name>" because there is no name to speak. The published claim is false on the product's own support channel.
recommendation: Add `aria-label` where a visible label would crowd the layout (chat-widget.tsx:1541 `aria-label="Message ${BOT_NAME}"`, support-tickets.tsx:609 and support-inbox.tsx:344 `aria-label="Reply"`, team-detail-header.tsx:79 `aria-label="Team name"`), and give history-notes.tsx:82 a real `useId()`-backed `<label htmlFor>` since it already has a visible "Notes" heading to reuse.

title: Five product surfaces the README advertises have no documentation page: billing and subscription management, bulk scanning, notifications, admin operations, and what to do when a scan fails or reports nothing
description: DOCS_NAV (components/docs/docs-nav.ts:13-140) has 19 entries across six sections. Cross-checking them against the shipped surface: (1) Billing. app/pricing, app/checkout, app/api/v3/billing/route.ts, app/api/v3/billing/subscription/cancel/route.ts and .../reactivate/route.ts exist, four paid plans are defined in lib/billing/catalog.ts, and three separate credit products have checkout components under components/billing/. No docs page explains plans, upgrading, cancelling, reactivating, credits, or what happens at the end of a trial; grepping app/docs for 'cancel' returns only API and team contexts and 'refund' returns one line on the AI page. (2) Bulk scanning. README.md:34 advertises it, app/api/v3/scan/bulk and components/scanner/dashboard-bulk-result.tsx implement it, and 'bulk scan' appears in app/docs only inside the API reference. (3) Notifications. app/api/v3/notifications exists and is referenced from eight docs pages in passing, with no page of its own. (4) Admin. app/admin plus 267 SETTINGS_REGISTRY entries, the audit log, impersonation, broadcasts, the Backup button and IP rules have no operator page; 'audit log' appears in app/docs only in the API reference and 'activity log' nowhere. (5) Troubleshooting a scan. Nothing anywhere covers a scan that fails, times out, or returns zero findings, which is the single most common support question for a scanner.
impact: Every one of these lands in support instead of self-service, and the project has in-app support tickets (app/docs/triage covers them) so the cost is real. Billing is the sharpest: a paying user who wants to cancel has no documentation and must find the button, which is a chargeback and trust risk on a service with a real subscriber base.
recommendation: Add three pages first, in this order: 'Plans and Billing' under Using VulnRadar (what each plan includes rendered from lib/billing/catalog.ts, how to upgrade, cancel and reactivate, how the three credit types work, what happens when a subscription lapses); 'Troubleshooting Scans' (timeouts, blocked targets, zero-finding results, robots.txt exclusions, what each terminal scan status means); and 'Administration' under Running your own (the /admin tabs, the settings registry, the audit log, backups, IP rules, impersonation). Fold bulk scanning into the scheduled-scans page or give it a section, and give notifications a section on the account-security page rather than a page of its own.

title: The product ships two mutually exclusive corner-radius conventions, so the scan result view and /profile are visibly different products sitting one nav item apart
description: audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md section C5 records the ladder: rounded-2xl for one flagship block, rounded-xl for content cards, code blocks, tables and the readout, rounded-lg for small cards and chip links, rounded-md for buttons. I counted every rounded-* literal per directory. components/scanner: 83 rounded-md, 4 rounded-lg, 0 rounded-xl. components/history: 21 rounded-md, 3 rounded-lg. components/shares, components/assets, components/host, components/teams and components/billing are the same shape (6, 6, 1, 10 and 36 rounded-md respectively). Against that, components/profile is 72 rounded-lg + 24 rounded-xl + 14 rounded-md, and components/admin is 132 rounded-lg + 19 rounded-xl + 26 rounded-md. These are not buttons: filtering to bordered card containers, the scanner family draws its panels at rounded-md (components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:608,719,837,862, dashboard.tsx:260,342,417,453, response-headers.tsx:46, dns-records-panel.tsx:207, port-scan-panel.tsx:126, threat-intel-panel.tsx, software-inventory-panel.tsx, results-list.tsx:463), while components/profile and components/admin draw the equivalent panels at rounded-lg or rounded-xl (18 and 9 of them respectively), and components/ui/card.tsx:12 (the shared primitive, used by 42 files) is rounded-lg. The landing page, the documented yardstick, uses rounded-xl for content cards. So the same nav bar leads to a 6px-radius scan report and a 12px-radius billing card.
impact: Radius is one of the two or three cues a person uses to decide whether two screens belong to the same application. A user who scans a site and then opens Profile crosses a visible seam. It also makes every new component a coin flip for the author, which is how the split got to 83 versus 132 in the first place.
recommendation: Adopt the landing ladder as written in design-language.md C5 and move the scanner family up, not the profile family down, because the shared primitive components/ui/card.tsx and 42 of its consumers are already on rounded-lg. Concretely: in components/scanner, change the bordered panel containers (issue-detail.tsx:608,719,837,862; dashboard.tsx:172,260,342,417,453; response-headers.tsx:46; dns-records-panel.tsx:207; port-scan-panel.tsx:126; results-list.tsx:463,598; scan-result-detail.tsx:228; crawl-pages-info.tsx:54; dashboard-error-state.tsx:182; scan-summary.tsx) from rounded-md to rounded-xl, and the same in components/history, components/shares, components/assets, components/host and components/teams. Leave rounded-md on the actual controls (inputs at results-list.tsx:379, buttons at :408,615) where it is correct. Then write the three-rung ladder into CLAUDE.md's spacing section so it is reviewable: rounded-xl = panel, rounded-lg = small card or chip, rounded-md = control, rounded-full = pill, rounded-2xl = one flagship block per page.

title: Seven different page-H1 treatments across 71 pages, and the documented Page H1 scale appears on no signed-in page at all
description: design-language.md B2 records the Page H1 (non-hero) as `text-3xl sm:text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight mb-5 text-balance`, cited from app/pricing/page.tsx:77. I extracted the className of every <h1> in app/ and components/. Seven distinct treatments ship: (1) the documented one, on app/pricing/page.tsx:77, app/checks/page.tsx:75, app/checks/category/[category]/page.tsx:126, app/alternatives/page.tsx:40, app/alternatives/[competitor]/page.tsx:85, app/tools/page.tsx:56, app/tools/api-scanner/page.tsx:79, app/tools/link-checker/page.tsx:80, all of them public SEO pages; (2) `text-xl sm:text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight text-foreground` on app/history/page.tsx:576, app/assets/page.tsx:148, app/shares/page.tsx:160, app/repos/page.tsx:360,465 and app/public-scans/page.tsx:118; (3) `text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight` on app/profile/page.tsx:679, app/admin/page.tsx:1021, app/attack-surface/page.tsx:30, app/legal/page.tsx:57 and app/teams/join/page.tsx:29; (4) `text-2xl sm:text-3xl font-semibold tracking-tight` on app/badge/page.tsx:101, app/changelog/page.tsx:22, app/compare/page.tsx:212, app/contact/page.tsx:56 and app/donate/page.tsx:32; (5) `text-lg font-semibold` with no tracking-tight on app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:144,161,218 and app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:143,251; (6) `font-bold` variants on app/checkout/credits/page.tsx:52,82,145 and its three sibling checkout pages, app/checkout/success/checkout-success-content.tsx:98 and app/security/page.tsx:48; (7) `text-2xl sm:text-4xl` (skipping the 3xl step) on app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:195. Only the SEO family matches the spec. Every page a paying user actually works in is on one of the other six. text-balance, which design-language.md B3 says goes on every heading, is present only on the SEO family, checks/[id] and two modal titles.
impact: A user moving Dashboard to History to Profile to Admin sees the page title change size three times for no reason, so nothing tells them what a page title is. Two of the seven treatments use font-bold, a weight design-language.md B3 records as appearing nowhere in the reference work.
recommendation: Two tiers, written down, then applied. Tier A (marketing, docs, SEO, legal, pricing): keep the documented `text-3xl sm:text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight mb-5 text-balance`. Tier B (in-app working pages, where the H1 sits above a dense table and must not eat the fold): standardise on `text-xl sm:text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight text-balance text-foreground`, which treatment (2) already uses on five pages and which is the largest existing cluster. Change app/profile/page.tsx:679, app/admin/page.tsx:1021, app/attack-surface/page.tsx:30, app/badge/page.tsx:101, app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:218 and app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:251 to Tier B, and app/security/page.tsx:48, app/legal/page.tsx:57, app/changelog/page.tsx:22, app/contact/page.tsx:56 and app/donate/page.tsx:32 to Tier A. Delete every font-bold in an <h1> (checkout pages are covered separately in dsn-05). Add both strings to CLAUDE.md under a Typography heading next to the existing Button and Spacing conventions, which is the only reason the button geometry stayed consistent and the heading scale did not.

title: The four checkout pages are the least spec-conformant surface in the product and they are the revenue path: container mx-auto, py-8 md:py-12, font-bold headings and md: breakpoints, all four times over
description: app/checkout/credits/page.tsx, app/checkout/github-credits/page.tsx, app/checkout/browser-credits/page.tsx and app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx (plus components/billing/checkout-skeleton.tsx) fail four of the fourteen tell-tale checks in design-language.md G simultaneously, and they are the only files in app/ that do. Check 2 (container): they are the only five files in the repo using Tailwind's `container` class, at credits:119,142, github-credits:121,140, browser-credits:123,142, [productId]:168,192 and checkout-skeleton:13,24, always as `container max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4`, where the documented default is `max-w-6xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6` and the responsive px step is missing. Check 1 (section rhythm): `py-8 md:py-12` at credits:142 and its three siblings, against the documented `py-16 sm:py-20`; md: rather than sm: is used for every breakpoint on these pages while the rest of app/ uses sm:. Check 7 (heading scale): `text-2xl font-bold mb-2` at credits:52,82, `text-2xl md:text-3xl font-bold mb-2` at :145, `text-lg font-bold` at :190 and `text-2xl font-bold` at :226, with the same lines in all three credit pages and [productId]:81,100,120,150,198,257. design-language.md B3 records that font-bold appears nowhere in the reference work. The three credit pages are otherwise near-identical files, which AUDIT-013#dup-06 already filed from the code-duplication angle (roughly 1,900 duplicated lines across the three checkout components and three pages); the design consequence is that a single fix has to be made three or four times and has not been.
impact: This is the screen where a user hands over a card. It is visibly heavier and more cramped than the pricing page they arrived from: a bolder title, half the vertical room, a narrower measure and no sm: padding step, so on a 640px phone the page has 16px gutters where /pricing has 24px. It reads as a different, older product at the exact moment trust matters most, and the same four defects have to be fixed four times because the pages were copied.
recommendation: Fix this together with AUDIT-013#dup-06's collapse rather than separately. When the three credit pages fold into one parameterised CreditCheckout page, give the surviving page: `<main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1} className="w-full max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6 py-12 sm:py-16">` (max-w-4xl is defensible for a single-task form; drop the `container` class, which does nothing here but add Tailwind's own padding), the Tier A page H1 from dsn-04 (`text-3xl sm:text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight mb-5 text-balance`), `text-lg font-semibold` for the tier price at credits:190, and `text-2xl font-semibold tabular-nums` for the Total today figure at :226. Change every md: breakpoint on these pages to sm: to match the rest of app/. Apply the same to app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx and components/billing/checkout-skeleton.tsx so the skeleton and the loaded page still line up.

title: Six implementations of one inline stat strip, at three different value type sizes and two container geometries, and two byte-identical copies of the STAT_ICON_TONES table
description: Extends AUDIT-013#dup-12, which caught the Cell duplication between components/assets/assets-stats.tsx:9 and components/shares/shares-stats.tsx:17 and the three identical stats skeletons, from the code angle. It missed four more copies and did not record the visual result. The full set: components/history/history-stats.tsx:18 defines a third byte-identical Cell; components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:94 defines StatCell (the same markup with items-start instead of items-center and no textTone); components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:75 defines Stat (same again at StatIcon size="sm" with a text-sm value and flex-1 basis-24 instead of a grid); components/admin/shared/stat-card.tsx:52 defines StatBar, a sixth. The value type size differs three ways for the same element: text-2xl in history-stats/assets-stats/shares-stats/dashboard.tsx:108, text-sm in scan-summary.tsx:88, text-lg in stat-card.tsx:82. The container differs two ways: `grid grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-4 gap-px bg-border overflow-hidden rounded-md border border-border` in the four app-side copies versus `flex flex-wrap rounded-lg border border-border/50 bg-border/50 gap-px overflow-hidden` at stat-card.tsx:62. On top of that, the STAT_ICON_TONES lookup is duplicated verbatim, nine keys and all their class strings, at components/shared/stat-icon.tsx:11-24 and components/admin/shared/stat-card.tsx:11-24; stat-icon.tsx's own docblock at :4-10 says it exists to stop each file inventing its own colours and then names stat-card.tsx as the pattern it is copying rather than importing from it.
impact: This is the mechanism by which one product stops looking like one product, applied to the element a user meets first on five different pages. The counts row on /dashboard, /history, /assets and /shares is 24px tall type in a 6px-radius box; the same row on /admin is 18px type in an 8px-radius box with a half-opacity border; the same row inside a scan summary is 14px type in a flex strip. Nothing distinguishes them semantically, so a reader learns the pattern four times. Two copies of the tone table mean the next colour added lands in one of them.
recommendation: Promote a single components/shared/stat-strip.tsx exporting `StatStrip({ items, size })` and reusing the existing StatIcon, with size="md" giving today's `text-2xl font-semibold leading-none tabular-nums tracking-tight` value and size="sm" giving `text-sm`, and one container: `flex flex-wrap gap-px overflow-hidden rounded-xl border border-border bg-border` (rounded-xl per dsn-03). Delete Cell from components/history/history-stats.tsx:18, components/assets/assets-stats.tsx:9 and components/shares/shares-stats.tsx:17, StatCell from components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:94, Stat from components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:75, and rewrite components/admin/shared/stat-card.tsx's StatBar as a thin wrapper that adds only the onClick/aria-pressed filtering behaviour its docblock at :46-51 describes. Delete the STAT_ICON_TONES block at components/admin/shared/stat-card.tsx:11-26 and import StatTone and the tones from components/shared/stat-icon.tsx. Collapse the three stats skeletons AUDIT-013#dup-12 lists into one StatStripSkeleton beside it so the loading state cannot drift from the loaded state again.

title: Five empty-state grammars, four of which are byte-identical wrappers around the same markup with a different icon and sentence
description: Five distinct empty-state treatments ship. (1) The app family, `flex flex-col items-center gap-3 rounded-md border border-dashed border-border bg-card/50 px-4 py-14 text-center` with a 6x6 icon at text-muted-foreground/60, a text-sm font-semibold title, a max-w-xs text-xs body and an optional sm Button: components/history/history-empty-state.tsx:25 and :48, components/assets/assets-empty-state.tsx:20 and :41, components/shares/shares-empty-state.tsx:7, components/public-scans/public-scans-empty-state.tsx:5, components/teams/teams-list.tsx:56 and :72, components/scanner/results-list.tsx:598, components/scanner/dashboard-results.tsx:269 and components/scanner/scan-result-detail.tsx:228. The four standalone files are the same JSX with only the icon and copy swapped, and each is its own module. (2) The admin family, components/admin/shared/data-table.tsx:19-45 EmptyState: no dashed border and no card at all, a 12x12 rounded-full bg-muted/50 circle holding a 6x6 icon at text-muted-foreground/50, py-16 px-4, text-sm font-medium title, text-xs max-w-sm body. Used by roughly 14 admin panels plus app/admin/page.tsx:1301,1502. (3) components/badge/badge-empty-state.tsx:8, `rounded-xl border border-dashed border-border bg-card/30 py-14 px-6`. (4) components/repos/repo-detail.tsx:251, `rounded-lg border border-dashed border-border px-4 py-10` with no background at all. (5) components/profile/tabs/developer/api-keys-section.tsx:250, `rounded-xl border border-dashed border-border bg-muted/20 p-5 sm:p-6` left-aligned. Radius spans md, lg and xl; the surface spans bg-card/50, bg-card/30, bg-muted/20 and nothing; the icon is bare in one family and in a circle in the other.
impact: Empty states are the first thing a new account sees on five pages in a row (/history, /assets, /shares, /teams, the results list) and they are the first thing an admin sees in fourteen panels. Two unrelated grammars for the same moment make the admin panel read as a bolted-on second application, which is exactly how it is built. Four separate one-file modules means a copy change or an a11y fix has to be made four times.
recommendation: Add components/shared/empty-state.tsx exporting `EmptyState({ icon, title, description, action, variant })` with the app family's geometry as the default (`flex flex-col items-center gap-3 rounded-xl border border-dashed border-border bg-card/50 px-4 py-14 text-center`, rounded-xl per dsn-03) and variant="inline" dropping the border and background for use inside a card that already has one, which is what the admin EmptyState is really doing. Delete components/history/history-empty-state.tsx, components/assets/assets-empty-state.tsx, components/shares/shares-empty-state.tsx and components/public-scans/public-scans-empty-state.tsx and call the shared component from the four pages with their icon and copy inline; delete the inline copies at components/teams/teams-list.tsx:56,72, components/scanner/results-list.tsx:598, dashboard-results.tsx:269 and scan-result-detail.tsx:228; re-export the shared component from components/admin/shared/data-table.tsx as EmptyState with variant="inline" so the fourteen admin call sites need no edit, and delete its body at :19-45. Fold components/badge/badge-empty-state.tsx and components/repos/repo-detail.tsx:251 in too.

title: Seven visual treatments for a row of tabs, only two of which use the Radix Tabs primitive, and /profile's sidebar is /admin's with the focus ring removed
description: Extends AUDIT-011#prof-01 (which filed /profile's mobile tab strip for having no accessible name below 640px) with the rest of the class. Seven treatments: (1) components/ui/tabs.tsx:16-33, a segmented control on `bg-muted p-1` with an active `bg-background shadow-xs` at rounded-sm, h-10, px-3 py-1.5, imported by exactly two files (components/admin/features/ip-rules-manager.tsx:29 and system-settings-manager.tsx:12); (2) components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:896-916, the same idiom hand-rolled at a different size, `flex gap-1 rounded-md bg-muted p-1` with active `bg-card shadow-xs`, rounded, px-2.5 py-1, text-xs; (3) app/assets/page.tsx:160-183, a third segmented variant, `inline-flex rounded-md border border-border bg-card p-0.5` with active `bg-primary text-primary-foreground`, a solid brand fill where the other two use a neutral raise; (4) components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx:29-44, underline tabs, `flex gap-1 border-b border-border/50` with `-mb-px border-b-2 border-primary px-3 py-2`, and no role or aria-current at all since they are Links; (5) components/docs/docs-code-tabs.tsx:30-47, underline plus fill plus top radius, `rounded-t-lg` with active `bg-secondary/30 border-b-2 border-primary`, px-4 py-2; (6) app/profile/page.tsx:723-739, the mobile strip, underline again but at px-3.5 py-3 with a `border-b border-border/80` rail rather than /50; (7) app/profile/page.tsx:743-768 and app/admin/page.tsx:1052-1097, the desktop vertical sidebar, `bg-primary/10 text-primary font-medium` pills at rounded-lg. Treatment (7) is nearly the same code twice: admin uses px-2.5 py-2 and includes `focus-visible:outline-hidden focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring` at :1076; profile uses px-3 py-2.5 and has no focus classes at all, so on /profile the eight sidebar links receive no visible focus except whatever the global :focus-visible rule at app/globals.css:370 supplies, and the sidebar widths differ (lg:w-48 versus lg:w-52).
impact: Tabs are the primary navigation idiom of the signed-in product and there is no such thing as "a tab" here. /assets renders its scope toggle as a solid blue pill, which under design-language.md's accent-restraint doctrine spends the page's one accent on a filter switch; two segmented controls that are visually the same are built two different ways so a keyboard fix lands on one; and the vertical sidebar that /profile and /admin share was copied rather than extracted, which is how /profile lost the explicit focus ring.
recommendation: Two shared components, not seven. (a) components/shared/segmented-control.tsx wrapping Radix Tabs with the components/ui/tabs.tsx:16 geometry plus a size prop ("sm" giving px-2.5 py-1 text-xs for dense use); replace components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:896 and app/assets/page.tsx:160 with it, and change the assets active state from bg-primary to the neutral `bg-background shadow-xs` raise the primitive already uses. (b) components/shared/section-nav.tsx holding the vertical sidebar markup currently duplicated at app/profile/page.tsx:743 and app/admin/page.tsx:1052, taking `items`, `groups` and `width`, with admin's focus-visible classes and admin's px-2.5 py-2, and use it on both pages. Keep the underline treatment for cross-page navigation only (components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx), give it `aria-current="page"` on the active Link, and switch components/docs/docs-code-tabs.tsx to the same underline geometry (drop rounded-t-lg and bg-secondary/30) so there is one underline tab and one segmented tab in the whole product. AUDIT-011#docs-11's tabpanel/aria-controls fix should land on (a) once, not on each copy.

title: Two callout components with overlapping variant names map warning to two different colours and use border-2, a width used nowhere else in the system
description:
components/docs/docs-callout.tsx:22-47 and components/legal/legal-callout.tsx:10-26 are two callout components with a `variant` prop whose vocabularies overlap but do not match: docs has info | warning | success | error, legal has warning | danger | info. `warning` exists in both and resolves to different colours: docs uses --warning (38 degrees) at :34-36, legal uses --severity-medium (45 degrees) at :12-14. `error` and `danger` are the same thing under two names. The geometry is unrelated too: docs is `rounded-r-lg border border-l-4 border-border/50 p-4` with a coloured left rule, a 3.5 icon and a text-xs font-semibold label, and its docblock at :14-19 explains the choice ("the left rule does the work; there is no icon-in-a-rounded-square, because four of those down a page is decoration"). Legal is `max-w-prose rounded-xl border-2 p-5` with no icon and a text-base font-semibold h3. border-2 appears on exactly one other non-decorative element in app/ and components/ (an avatar ring and a spinner), so it is a one-off width. Both are correct on tokens, so this is purely a grammar split. It also produces a heading-level inconsistency: the legal callout emits an

inside legal sections that already have their own h3s, while the docs callout emits a

.
impact: A reader who goes from /docs/self-hosting (which uses the docs callout heavily) to /legal/acceptable-use sees the same kind of aside drawn with a different border weight, a different radius, no icon and no coloured rule, and the warning aside changes hue. The duplicated vocabulary also means a future "add a note about X" ticket gets two different implementations depending on which directory it lands in.
recommendation:
Delete components/legal/legal-callout.tsx and re-export DocsCallout from components/shared/callout.tsx (moved out of components/docs/ since two sections use it), mapping the two legal call sites: app/legal/acceptable-use/page.tsx:51 variant="warning" stays warning, app/legal/dmca/page.tsx:62 variant="info" stays info, and app/security/page.tsx:63 variant="info" stays info. Keep the docs geometry and the four-variant vocabulary (info | warning | success | error), since it is the one with a written rationale and 60-odd call sites. Add an optional `as="h3"` prop if a legal callout genuinely needs to be a heading in the document outline; otherwise leave it as the

label the docs version uses. Retire the name `danger`.

title: The profile Social tab and the two OAuth profile modals are a brand-chrome island: full-bleed vendor gradients, decorative white blobs, text-white and font-bold, unlike anything else in the app
description: components/profile/tabs/profile-social-tab.tsx:604 opens the Discord card with `relative bg-linear-to-br from-[#5865F2] via-[#4752C4] to-[#3C45A5] px-6 py-5` and :777 opens the GitHub card with `relative bg-linear-to-br from-[#24292e] via-[#1b1f23] to-[#0d1117] px-6 py-5`, both with `titleClassName="text-white"` and `subtitleClassName="text-white/70"`, a `h-10 w-10 rounded-xl bg-white` icon plate at :154, a `bg-white/15 backdrop-blur-xs ring-1 ring-white/20` plate at :607 and a `bg-white/20 text-white border-white/30` badge at :622. components/modals/discord-profile-modal.tsx:90-125 and components/modals/github-profile-modal.tsx:97-125 go further: a full-bleed brand header, three absolutely positioned `rounded-full bg-white/20` decorative circles at :92-94 and :99-101, a `border-4 border-background ring-4` avatar at :120, `text-xl font-bold text-white` at :107 and `text-2xl font-bold` at :125. Nowhere else in app/ or components/ is there a gradient header, a decorative blob, a border-4 ring or text-white outside a scrim. The rest of the product paints on bg-card with a border and spends colour on one element per section. The literal hexes are legitimate third-party brand colours (design-language.md A3 permits them), so the problem is not the values, it is the composition: five nested branded surfaces to say "you can sign in with Discord".
impact: /profile is one of the two or three most-visited signed-in pages, and its Social tab looks like a different design system dropped into a slot. The gradient headers also make the two cards the loudest thing on a page whose actual content (2FA, API keys, billing) is quieter, so visual weight is inverted against importance. The three floating white circles are pure decoration in a product whose illustration doctrine (design-language.md E2) is "the actual mechanism of the product, rendered as itself".
recommendation: Bring both cards back to the house grammar and keep the brand colour as a single accent. Replace the gradient header at profile-social-tab.tsx:604 and :777 with the standard card header used elsewhere in the tab tree, `flex items-center gap-3 border-b border-border/60 px-5 py-4`, holding a `h-9 w-9 rounded-lg` plate filled with the vendor colour (bg-[#5865F2] / bg-[#181717]) and the vendor glyph in white, then `text-base font-semibold text-foreground` for the label and `text-xs text-muted-foreground` for the subtitle; that keeps the brand recognisable in exactly one element per card. Drop titleClassName / subtitleClassName / headerClassName from the OAuthIdentityCard props entirely once both callers stop overriding them. Keep the connect button's brand fill at :721 and :780 (it is the one action that should read as the vendor's) but drop shadow-xs. In components/modals/discord-profile-modal.tsx and github-profile-modal.tsx, delete the six decorative `bg-white/20` circles at :92-94 and :99-101, replace the gradient header with the same bordered header, change `text-xl font-bold text-white` to `text-lg font-semibold text-foreground` and `border-4 ... ring-4` to `ring-2 ring-border`.

title: One static OG image serves every page on the site, so a shared scan, a check page and the pricing page all unfurl identically
description: app/layout.tsx:69-84 is the only `openGraph` block in the entire app/ tree (verified by grep across app/ for both .ts and .tsx), and it points every page at the single static `/og-image.png` built by scripts/build-og-image.mjs from public/og-image.svg. There are zero `opengraph-image.tsx` or `twitter-image.tsx` route files anywhere under app/. That means /shared/[token], /host/[hostname], /compare, /pricing, all 20 /docs sections and the roughly 750 /checks SEO pages every unfurl with the same card, whose baked copy reads "Scan any website for security issues in seconds. Just a URL." over a mock result for "your-domain.com" showing a risk score of 2 and five invented findings. The card itself is strong work (audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md names it one of the three best artifacts in the repo) and it is right for the site root, but it is the only card that exists.
impact: Sharing a scan is a core flow, and the share link is the product's main organic distribution: a user pastes /shared/<token> into a Slack channel or a ticket, and everyone who sees it gets a generic marketing card for a fictional domain instead of the hostname and the finding counts they were being shown. The same applies to the roughly 750 /checks pages, which are the main organic SEO surface: every one of them competes for the same unfurl, so nothing in a search or social preview distinguishes "Missing HSTS" from "Exposed .git directory". This compounds AUDIT-012#fe-01, which already found only 5 of 311 routes prerendered.
recommendation: Add three `opengraph-image.tsx` route files using next/og ImageResponse, all rendering one shared layout so they read as a family with the existing SVG (bg #0a0e18 to #0e1526, card #141d30, stroke #26344d, mono wordmark top-left, headline in #ffffff with the accent clause in #60a5fa, severity dots straight from the --severity-* scale exactly as og-image.svg:93-101 already does). (1) app/shared/[token]/opengraph-image.tsx: the scanned hostname as the headline, the risk score chip, and one severity distribution bar with the real counts, all read from the same share query the page uses. (2) app/checks/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx: the check title, its severity chip, and its category, from the checks registry. (3) app/host/[hostname]/opengraph-image.tsx: the hostname and its current reputation score. Set `export const size = { width: 1200, height: 630 }` and `alt` on each. Keep the static PNG as the root and docs fallback. Because ImageResponse only supports a subset of CSS, build it as flex boxes with explicit widths, and load no external font: the site already ships in system-ui (AUDIT-011#design-02), so next/og's default is consistent with the product rather than a deviation.

title: app/global-error.tsx is a different design from the other two error pages: different palette, no wordmark, no status numeral, no digest, and no light mode
description: app/error.tsx and app/not-found.tsx are the same composition: a mono wordmark lockup with ThemedLogo, a `border-y border-border/50 py-8` band holding a `font-mono text-6xl font-semibold tabular-nums` status numeral (500 / 404), a short honest sentence, a two-up button row, and a row of three or two `text-primary` footer links, all on tokens and all with `focus.ring` (error.tsx:33-127, not-found.tsx:15-89). app/global-error.tsx shares none of it: it opens with a 6rem circle holding a warning icon at :51-60 (an icon-in-a-rounded-shape, which CLAUDE.md and design-language E1 name as an anti-pattern), has no wordmark at all, no numeral, no error.digest block despite error.digest being available in its props, and it hardcodes `#09090b` / `#fafafa` / `#a1a1aa` / `#71717a` / `#52525b`, which is the Tailwind zinc ramp, not the app's #0C0E12 / #F0F2F5 navy. Its two links are coloured `BRAND_TEAL = "#0891b2"` (:10), a brand the product no longer has. It is also dark-only: a light-mode user hitting the global boundary drops into a black page. Inline styles there are correct and the file's own comment (:6-9) explains why, but the values are wrong, and nothing forces the two files to stay in sync. Separately, both error.tsx:103 and not-found.tsx:47 label the secondary route back as "Go to Dashboard", which is the product's internal noun for what an anonymous visitor arriving on a 404 from a search engine experiences as the scan page.
impact: The global boundary is the page a user sees when the app has failed hardest, and it is the one that looks least like the product: teal links on zinc, no logo, no error id to quote to support. A user who does reach it cannot copy a digest, so a support conversation starts with "it broke" and no correlation id. The publicly reachable and indexable 404 sends an anonymous visitor to a button labelled with a word that only means something to an existing user.
recommendation: Rebuild app/global-error.tsx as a literal-hex mirror of app/error.tsx rather than a separate design. Keep the inline-style constraint, but source the values from lib/config/brand.ts by transcribing them with a comment pointing back: background #0b0e14, card #12151c, border #252a34, text #f1f5f9, muted #9aa6b8, link #60a5fa (delete BRAND_TEAL). Add a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light)` block via a small inline `<style>` element in the same file so the light palette (#dfe5ec / #eff2f5 / #14181f) is available without CSS variables. Replace the 6rem icon circle with the same structure error.tsx uses: an inline SVG VulnRadar mark plus the wordmark in `ui-monospace` at 20px/600, a 1px top and bottom rule at rgba(255,255,255,0.08), a monospace 60px "500", the heading "Something broke on our end", and the digest in a bordered mono block with a copy button (navigator.clipboard, guarded). Add a comment in both files naming the other as the sibling that must match. Separately, change the secondary CTA label in both error.tsx:105 and not-found.tsx:49 from "Go to Dashboard" to "Scan a URL", which is what the page actually does and matches the voice rule that copy names the mechanism.

title: The web surface ships zero screenshots of the application, and the five finished 533x333 store screenshots in extension/public/store are referenced by no page, route, or asset in the repo
description: Grepping app/, components/, public/, lib/ and scripts/ for "store_" returns zero matches outside extension/public/store itself, so store_1.png through store_5.png are used only in the Chrome Web Store and AMO listings. public/ contains exactly six files (favicon.ico, favicon.png, favicon.svg, gitlab, og-image.png, og-image.svg) and no product imagery. components/landing/ and app/landing/ contain zero next/image imports, zero , and zero .png/.jpg/.webp references. What the landing page does show is genuinely good and should not be discarded: components/shared/response-readout.tsx renders a live request/response readout in the hero, and components/landing/landing-sample-finding.tsx:59-107 hand-builds a complete finding card in JSX with real evidence and a real Nginx and Express fix. So the gap is not "the output is never shown", the output is shown well. The gap is that nothing shows the application: the dashboard, the history list, the two-scan diff at /compare that components/landing/landing-features.tsx:34-36 leans on as its closing argument, or the extension that is live on two stores. The five unused PNGs are, per audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md section E3, one of the three strongest visual artefacts in the repo, with an established composition (alternating side, two-tone white and #60a5fa headline, mono footnote, real UI over a browser-chrome mock).
impact: A security scanner's report is its product, and a visitor deciding between this and a commercial scanner has no way to see whether the application is a real product or a landing page with an API behind it. Trust for an unknown vendor with roughly 50 users is bought largely with evidence that the thing exists. Meanwhile finished, on-brand art that cost real design effort reaches only Chrome Web Store browsers and never the site.
recommendation: Copy extension/public/store/*.png to public/store/ and add five specific images to the web surface. (1) A full completed report from /dashboard, placed as a full-bleed band directly after the hero, showing the verdict header, the SeverityDistribution bar from components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:129-190, and the first four findings collapsed. This is the missing "the product exists" proof. (2) A real screenshot of IssueDetail expanded on hsts-missing, replacing the hand-built <article> at landing-sample-finding.tsx:59-107 while keeping its left column copy verbatim: the JSX version is a drawing of the product, the screenshot is the product. (3) The /compare two-scan diff, added as a small figure inside components/landing/landing-features.tsx's accent block, because "what makes the diff between Tuesday and Friday readable" (:34-36) is the one claim the page argues hardest and never shows. (4) store_1.png reused as-is on a new /extension marketing page and in app/docs/extension/page.tsx. (5) The dashboard scan form with the category selector open, next to landing-categories.tsx:30-32's claim that checks are gated to the URL types they apply to. Use next/image with explicit width and height, wrap each in a rounded-xl border border-border/60 to match the card grammar in design-language.md D1, and give each a real alt describing the finding shown, not "screenshot".

title: Every honest trust signal the project owns is unlinked from the marketing surface: the public scan directory, the comparison pages, the 754 check pages, the free tools, the security page and the committed audit history
description: What exists and is verifiable: /public-scans, a directory of real scans users chose to publish (app/public-scans/page.tsx, public per lib/config/public-paths.ts); /alternatives, five honest comparison pages whose own copy commits to "No invented competitor prices, no disparagement" (app/alternatives/page.tsx:47-48); roughly 754 /checks pages, each a real rule with its own fix guide; /tools, two free tools; /security plus /.well-known/security.txt; SECURITY-POSTURE.md, a public self-hardening checklist that opens with "We ship a scanner that grades other people's domains, so our own domain has to pass its own checks"; a live dogfood badge in README.md:18 pointing at a permanent shared report of vulnradar.dev; fourteen self-audits committed in audits/ (verified tracked with git ls-files, not ignored); a changelog; GPL-3.0; "Telemetry: None"; two live store listings. What links to any of it from the marketing surface: grepping components/landing/, app/landing/ and components/scanner/footer.tsx for "/checks", "/public-scans", "PUBLIC_SCANS", "/alternatives" and "/tools" returns zero matches. /public-scans is linked only from components/scanner/header.tsx (the logged-in app header) and two docs pages. components/scanner/footer.tsx:60-107's Product column lists Scanner, History, Compare and Badges, of which Scanner and History both require a session, so a logged-out visitor's footer is mostly redirects to /login. components/landing/landing-categories.tsx renders all eighteen categories as a table with counts and blurbs and not one cell is a link, so the highest-authority page on the site sends no traffic and no link equity into the 754-page check surface it is describing.
impact: For a security product from an unknown vendor, trust is the purchase. This project has an unusually strong honest-signal inventory for its size, including a committed audit history and a published self-hardening checklist, and a visitor is shown none of it. Separately, the roughly 780 SEO pages have no inbound link from the landing page, so the main organic surface is orphaned from the site's strongest page.
recommendation: Do not invent social proof, surface what exists. (1) Make every category row in components/landing/landing-categories.tsx link to /checks/category/{key}, both in the sm:hidden card list at :42-79 and the table at :81-146, and add a "See all {total} checks" link to /checks beside the count at :34-39. That is eighteen internal links from the site's strongest page into the SEO surface, and it makes the section clickable proof rather than a static table. (2) Add a Resources footer entry for /public-scans labelled "Public scans" and one for /alternatives labelled "Compared to other scanners", and a Product entry for /tools labelled "Free tools", in components/scanner/footer.tsx:60-150. (3) Extend the FACTS <dl> in components/landing/landing-open-source.tsx:6-13 with two rows that are the strongest available and currently invisible: ["Our own last scan", "Public, permanent report"] linking the shared report README.md:18 already uses, and ["Self-audits", "14, committed in the repo"] linking audits/ on GitHub. Verify the shared-report link still resolves before publishing it. (4) Note the honest caveat: /public-scans is opt-in and its empty state (components/public-scans/public-scans-empty-state.tsx:9) says "No public scans yet", so check it has content before linking it from the landing page, and seed it by publishing the team's own scans first.

title: There is no command palette and no keyboard shortcut layer anywhere in a developer tool with eight top-level sections
description: A repo-wide grep for cmdk, CommandDialog, useHotkeys and global keydown handlers finds no command palette and no application-level shortcut registration. The only document-level keydown listeners in app/ and components/ are modal Escape and focus trapping (lib/hooks/use-modal-a11y.ts:54 and :91), the AI chat widget's own textarea handling (components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:833 and :1070), and two mobile nav overlays (components/docs/docs-mobile-nav.tsx:58, components/admin/shared/admin-mobile-toc.tsx:140). There is no global search either: components/scanner/header.tsx renders logo, eight nav links (:25-34), a notification bell, a theme toggle and log out, with no search input at any breakpoint. app/docs has no search of any kind: components/docs/docs-sidebar.tsx and docs-shell.tsx contain no input element.
impact: Reaching a past scan means navigating to History and typing into a filter that only covers the newest 100 rows. Reaching scheduled scans means Profile, then the Developer tab, then the Schedules sub-tab. Reaching one check's documentation means /checks, expanding one of eighteen accordions, then browser find. Each of these is a single fuzzy-search entry for the audience this product targets, and its absence is the most visible way the app reads as less finished than the landing page that sells it.
recommendation: Add a Cmd/Ctrl-K palette mounted next to <Toaster /> in app/layout.tsx. cmdk is the conventional choice and the repo already uses Radix throughout, so components/ui/dialog.tsx supplies the shell. Seed it with five groups: Navigate, from the NAV_LINKS array at components/scanner/header.tsx:25-34 plus the profile tab list at app/profile/page.tsx:625-665; Actions (New scan, Compare scans, New API key, New schedule); Scans, hitting the server-side history search from qolf-01, matched on URL and tag; Checks, over the static registry that already backs app/checks/page.tsx, jumping to /checks/{id}; and Docs, over the tree in components/docs/docs-nav.ts. Then add a shortcut sheet on `?` and the three shortcuts that matter on a results page: `/` to focus the findings search (components/scanner/results-list.tsx:372), j and k to move between findings, Escape to return to the list.

title: There is no undo anywhere in the product, and clearing all history is a single icon button beside the search box
description: A repo-wide grep for undo across app/, components/ and lib/ returns five hits and none is an undo affordance: three are code comments, one is a docs sentence stating there is no undo (app/docs/account-security/page.tsx:503), and one is an unsaved-state toggle label in the admin badge editor (components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:1198). Every destructive path is therefore confirm-then-permanent. Clear all history deletes every scan on the account in one DELETE (app/history/page.tsx:280-295, dialog :640-694) and its trigger is a single icon button sitting immediately beside the search input in the filter row (components/history/history-filters.tsx:76-88). Delete scan removes the scan, its findings and its notes (components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:505-515). Remove member, Delete team, Delete schedule and Delete webhook are the same shape (app/teams/page.tsx:340 and :250, components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:388 and :368).
impact: Clear all history is the one that will eventually cost a user everything they have, and it is two clicks from a control adjacent to the search box they use constantly. For a product whose entire value is that finding IDs are stable across runs so a diff between two scans means something, losing the history destroys the diff, and there is nothing to recover from.
recommendation: Add a soft-delete window for the three that need it most, in this order. (1) Clear all history: add a deleted_at column to scan_history, have the DELETE handler stamp it rather than delete, exclude stamped rows from the list query at app/api/v3/history/route.ts:117-142, and show a persistent "Cleared 143 scans. Undo" bar for 30 seconds after the dialog closes, purging stamped rows on the existing retention sweep. (2) Delete scan: same mechanism surfaced as an undo toast (qolf-07). (3) Remove team member: re-adding is possible via invite but loses their scan association, so stamp and offer undo. Once undo exists for an action, drop that action's confirmation dialog: an undo bar plus an AlertDialog for the same action is one interruption too many. Also move the Clear All button out of the filter row into a danger section below the list, away from the search input it currently sits beside.

title: No search or filter state anywhere in the app is URL-backed, so opening a finding and pressing Back silently resets every filter you set
description: lib/ui/url-state.ts provides a complete solution including the LOCATION_CHANGE_EVENT bridge (:19-49) and a useQueryParam hook (:170), but that hook has only two consumers repo-wide: app/repos/page.tsx:134 and components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx. Everywhere else `page` and `scope` are hand-wired into the URL while every search box and filter is plain useState: components/scanner/results-list.tsx:114-120 (severity set, category, sort direction, grouping, search), app/history/page.tsx:66-67 and :72, app/teams/page.tsx:49, app/assets/page.tsx:35, app/compare/page.tsx:37, app/admin/page.tsx:197. The findings list is the sharp case: selecting a finding calls setQueryParam(FINDING_QUERY_PARAM, issue.id) with the default pushState at components/scanner/results-list.tsx:273, creating a history entry, and both host pages swap ResultsList out for IssueDetail (app/history/page.tsx:465-473). Pressing Back unmounts IssueDetail, remounts ResultsList, and every filter returns to its default at :114-120, while scroll position is deliberately preserved across that same remount at :262-267.
impact: Reviewing a scan goes: filter to Critical and High, open the first finding, read it, press Back, and the list is unfiltered again while the scroll position is restored to where you were in the shorter filtered list, dropping you at an arbitrary offset in a longer one. On a 200-finding crawl that happens on every single finding. Nothing filtered can be shared or bookmarked either: a link to "the criticals on this scan" or "my staging scans" does not exist.
recommendation: Swap the useState declarations for the useQueryParam hook that already exists. In components/scanner/results-list.tsx:114-120 back sev, cat, sort, group and q with query params, omitting each when it equals its default so a clean scan URL stays clean, and write them with { replace: true } so filter changes do not pollute the back stack (the finding param at :273 keeps pushState, which is correct). Do the same for filter and tag in app/history/page.tsx:66-67 and the search state in app/teams/page.tsx:49, app/assets/page.tsx:35 and app/compare/page.tsx:37. Also add LOCATION_CHANGE_EVENT to the two page-sync effects that listen only for QUERY_CHANGE_EVENT and popstate, app/public-scans/page.tsx:99-100 and app/assets/page.tsx:60-61, since clicking their own tab in components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx while already on that page at ?page=3 is exactly the soft-navigation case the bridge was written for and which app/history/page.tsx:213 already handles.

title: There is no path from a finding you just fixed back to verifying it: no rescan on the issue view, and Compare is reachable only from the top nav
description: components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx renders a full remediation lifecycle (Open / In progress / Fixed, persisted at :349 and keyed on the stable finding id per the docblock at :253-259) but contains no action that re-runs the scan or re-checks that finding. The only rescan in the product is the history row menu, which is desktop-only and a no-op (qolf-02, qolf-03). Compare is linked from exactly two places, components/scanner/header.tsx:29 and components/scanner/footer.tsx:85, never from a scan or a finding. Reaching a diff from an open finding is: back to the findings list, back to history, Compare in the nav, find the host in the picker (app/compare/page.tsx:238), pick two scans if the host has more than two (:268), press Compare (:276). Six interactions, and the host you were just looking at is not preselected.
impact: Find, fix, verify is the loop this product exists to serve, and verify is the only leg with no direct route. In practice users mark a finding Fixed and never confirm it, which makes the remediation status a self-reported label rather than a verified one, and leaves the strongest claim the product makes ("the same URL produces the same finding IDs and the same ratings on every run, which is the only reason a diff between two scans means anything", components/landing/landing-how-it-works.tsx:32-35) unreachable from inside the product.
recommendation: Add two entries. First, a "Re-check this" button on the issue detail beside the remediation control at components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:829: it runs the same scan the dashboard does against result.url, polls status, and on completion reports whether this finding id is present in the new run, then offers "Open the new scan" and "Mark fixed". Second, add "Compare with previous scan" to the scan actions menu (components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:532-661, beside the existing Share entry), resolving the previous scan for the same host server-side and navigating straight to /compare?a=<prev>&b=<current>, which app/compare/page.tsx:72-93 already accepts as a deep link. Both collapse six interactions to one and both reuse existing endpoints.

title: The Developer nav entry that made scheduled scans discoverable is dead code: DEVELOPER_HREF is not in NAV_LINKS, so 25 lines of header logic can never run
description: components/scanner/header.tsx:23 defines DEVELOPER_HREF as `${ROUTES.PROFILE}?tab=developer` under a comment at :18-22 explaining that scheduled scans, webhooks, domains and API keys "had no top-level entry, so recurring monitoring, the whole point of a scheduled scan, was two clicks deep under Profile and effectively undiscoverable". NAV_LINKS at :25-34 lists eight entries and DEVELOPER_HREF is not one of them. Consequently handleNavClick (:69-79) always returns at its first line `if (href !== DEVELOPER_HREF) return`, because no rendered link ever equals that constant; the `if (href === DEVELOPER_HREF)` branch in isNavActive (:82) is unreachable; and the locationSearch state with its popstate and QUERY_CHANGE_EVENT effect (:45-58) plus the onDeveloperTab derivation (:59-60) exist only to feed that unreachable branch.
impact: Scheduled scans, webhooks, verified domains and API keys are back to three navigations deep with no top-level entry, which the code comment itself identifies as the problem this was supposed to fix. Recurring monitoring is the feature that turns a one-off scanner into something a team keeps paying for, and nothing in the product's chrome points at it. Twenty-five lines of header code also carry maintenance cost and read as intentional to the next person editing the file.
recommendation: Add { href: DEVELOPER_HREF, label: "Developer" } to NAV_LINKS at components/scanner/header.tsx:25-34, which restores every code path in the file. Nine desktop items is one too many for the absolutely-centred nav at :153, so move Badge (:32) into the Developer tab where it belongs, since it is a per-scan embed rather than a section. If the entry is genuinely not wanted, delete DEVELOPER_HREF, handleNavClick, the locationSearch state and effect, and the onDeveloperTab derivation rather than leaving them, and surface schedules another way, for example a "Schedule this scan" entry in the scan actions menu that deep-links to /profile?tab=developer&dtab=schedules with the URL prefilled.

title: No user-facing list in the product has a sort control, and history has no severity, date-range or source filter despite carrying all three fields
description: components/history/history-filters.tsx renders exactly three controls: a URL search box (:36), a tag dropdown (:46) and Clear All (:76). Repo-wide only four files contain any sort state (components/scanner/results-list.tsx, components/admin/features/ai-chats-manager.tsx, components/admin/features/ip-rules-manager.tsx, components/admin/staff/staff-list.tsx) and only the first is on a non-admin surface. Every user list is therefore locked to a fixed server order: history ORDER BY sh.scanned_at DESC (app/api/v3/history/route.ts:127), shares ORDER BY scanned_at DESC (app/api/v3/shares/route.ts:28), assets ORDER BY last_scanned_at DESC (app/api/v3/assets/route.ts:141), public scans ORDER BY sh.scanned_at DESC (app/api/v3/public-scans/route.ts:94). Yet the history row already renders per-severity counts from s.summary (components/history/history-scan-row.tsx:57-72) and the API already selects sh.source (app/api/v3/history/route.ts:119) and never exposes it.
impact: "Show me every scan that turned up a critical" and "show me last week" are the two questions a security team asks of a scan history, and neither is answerable, so triage is scroll-and-read.
