Two defaults are also on the wrong axis: /shares sorts by when the underlying scan ran rather than when the link was created or expires, and /assets sorts by most-recently-scanned, which surfaces the host you already know about and buries the stale one, when "not scanned in N days" is the single most useful view of an asset inventory.
recommendation: On the history filter row add a severity segmented filter (Any / Critical / High and above / Clean) derived from s.summary, a date-range select (Last 7 days / 30 days / All), a source filter over the source column the API already returns, and a sort select (Newest, Worst severity, Most findings, Host A-Z). Push all of them into SQL alongside the server-side search from qolf-01 rather than filtering the capped client array. Change the /assets default order at app/api/v3/assets/route.ts:141 to stalest-first or add an explicit "Needs a rescan" filter, and order /shares by share creation. Back all of it with useQueryParam per qolf-10 so a filtered view is linkable. On mobile these do not fit inline, so put them behind one "Filters" trigger opening components/ui/sheet.tsx with the active-filter count on the trigger.

title: A new account meets an eight-step feature-tour modal before it can reach the scan box, and the tour's copy is exactly the generic voice CLAUDE.md bans
description: OnboardingTour is mounted first in the dashboard tree (app/dashboard/page.tsx:876) and opens on any account where onboardingCompleted is false (components/shared/onboarding-tour.tsx:83-92), rendering a full-screen backdrop at :122. STEPS at :24-77 is eight entries. The signup-to-first-scan path is already landing, signup form, verification email, verify page which auto-redirects after a 2 second timer (app/verify-email/VerifyEmailClient.tsx:76-79), and then this modal. The copy is generic in exactly the ways CLAUDE.md and audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md section F prohibit: "Your all-in-one web vulnerability scanner. Let's walk you through the key features so you can get the most out of VulnRadar" (:28), "Great for verifying that you fixed vulnerabilities" (:46), "You're All Set!" (:71), against a landing page whose voice is "Paste a URL. Get findings, not a grade out of ten." (components/auth/auth-split-layout.tsx:105-107).
impact: The first thing a new user sees inside the product is eight screens of feature marketing about teams, webhooks and CI integration, none of which they can evaluate before running one scan. Skipping is one click, so most users will skip and learn nothing, and the ones who do not spend eight clicks before reaching the box. It is also the first impression that contradicts the landing page's voice, which is the strongest work in the repo.
recommendation: Delete the blocking modal and let the account land on the scan form, which components/scanner/scan-hero.tsx already introduces. Replace it with two cheaper things. First, a single dismissible strip above the form for a brand-new account, in the landing page's voice, along the lines of "Paste any URL. Nothing to install: the request goes out from our servers, not your browser." Second, one-time contextual hints attached to the features they describe and shown after the moment each becomes relevant: a "Compare this against your last run" pointer the second time the same host is scanned, an "API keys and schedules live here" pointer the first time the Developer tab opens. The existing POST /api/v3/auth/onboarding completion flag (:96) and the tour-replay entry at components/profile/tabs/profile-general-tab.tsx:441 can both stay, with the replay opening a static "What's here" page instead of a wizard. The step list at :139-203, which shows the whole shape at once and lets you jump anywhere, is the good part and is worth keeping as that page.

title: Four signed-in pages open with the same four-cell aggregate strip, and on /history three of its four cells are derivable from the other one and from the heading directly above it
description:
The identical container `grid grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-4 gap-px bg-border overflow-hidden rounded-md border border-border` opens four pages: /dashboard (components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:148 and :261), /history (components/history/history-stats.tsx:66), /shares (components/shares/shares-stats.tsx:64) and /assets (components/assets/assets-stats.tsx:53). All four hold four cells built from a `Cell` or `StatCell` function with the same body: a StatIcon, a `text-2xl font-semibold tabular-nums` number and an `text-[11px] text-muted-foreground` label. Adjacent pages therefore open with an identical template, which is what CLAUDE.md's layout-patterns-to-avoid list and design-language.md tell-tale 6 call out.

On /history it is also redundant content. The h1 subtitle at app/history/page.tsx:579-585 already reads `{scans.length} scans on record`, and the very next element, HistoryStats at :588, opens with a Total scans cell holding the same `scans.length` (history-stats.tsx:55, :67-72). Of the remaining three cells, Came back clean (:56) and Had findings (:57) are complementary filters of the same array and sum back to the first cell, so three of the four numbers carry no information the reader did not already have. Only Findings total (:58-61) is new.
impact: Every signed-in list page looks like every other signed-in list page above the fold, and the strip costs a screenful before the reader reaches the thing the page is for. On /history specifically the reader is shown the same number twice in adjacent elements.
recommendation:
Keep the strip where it earns its place and vary the others, following the nine-different-layouts principle the landing page demonstrates.

- /history: delete HistoryStats entirely (remove the import and the call at app/history/page.tsx:588, delete components/history/history-stats.tsx and its skeleton branch). Fold the one number worth keeping into the existing subtitle at :579-585: `{n} scans on record, {m} findings across them, kept for {retention}`. That removes a component and a screenful and loses nothing.
- /shares: replace the four cells with the SeverityDistribution bar from components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:129-190, whose own docblock explains it reads as one bar rather than five cards. Clean, warnings and unsafe are proportions of one whole, which is exactly what that component is for.
- /assets: same substitution, the four cells are Hosts scanned plus a three-way safety split.
- /dashboard: keep the strip. It is the one page where four independent counters are the right shape, and it is already paired with the activity sparkline rather than standing alone.

title: The domain portfolio UI renders at two URLs because the move to /attack-surface never removed the copy in the profile Developer tab
description:
DomainsSection (components/profile/tabs/developer/domains-section.tsx:97, 515 lines) has two importers. app/attack-surface/page.tsx:54 renders it as a top-level page reached from the HistoryViewTabs strip, and that file's own doc comment at :12-14 states the reason: the domain-verification UI already existed but was buried in the profile Developer tab, so this surfaces it as its own tab. components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx still lists it as a fourth sub-tab at :82 and still renders it at :754, reachable at /profile?tab=developer&dtab=domains.

The two surfaces are the same component with different chrome: /attack-surface gives it an h1, an explanatory paragraph about what verifying a domain unlocks, and the History/Assets/Attack Surface/Public Scans tab strip; the profile copy gives it a sub-tab label and nothing else. Verifying a domain from one and then opening the other shows two independently fetched copies of the same list.
impact: Two URLs for one feature, so a user who bookmarks or is linked to one never discovers the other, and the profile copy is the worse of the two because it has none of the explanatory framing that tells the user what domain verification is for. It also doubles the maintenance surface: any change to the surrounding affordances has to be made twice or the two drift.
recommendation: Finish the move. Delete the `{ id: "domains", label: "Domains", icon: ShieldCheck }` entry from DEVELOPER_SECTIONS at components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:82 and the `{activeSection === "domains" && ...}` branch at :754, and drop domains from the DeveloperSection type. In its place put a one-line pointer in the Developer tab's header, `Verified domains moved to Attack surface`, linking to ROUTES.ATTACK_SURFACE, so anyone with the old deep link lands somewhere useful. Add a redirect from ?tab=developer&dtab=domains to /attack-surface in the dtab handling at app/profile/page.tsx:110-120 for the same reason.

title: Scheduled scans and webhooks sit three levels deep under Account Settings while Badge, a one-time embed snippet, is a top-level nav item
description:
The signed-in nav (components/scanner/header.tsx:26-33) has eight entries: Scanner, History, Repos, Compare, Shared, Teams, Badge, Profile. Badge is /badge, a page that generates an embeddable status badge snippet, which a user configures once and never returns to. It sits at the same level as History.

Scheduled Scans, the product's recurring-monitoring feature with its own documentation section at app/docs/scheduled-scans, is at /profile?tab=developer&dtab=schedules: Profile in the nav, then the Developer tab (app/profile/page.tsx:645-651), then the Scheduled Scans sub-tab (profile-developer-tab.tsx:81). Three levels, and the page it lives on is titled Account Settings (app/profile/page.tsx:679). Webhooks are in the same place (:80). Both are things a user returns to, filed under settings; the header's DEVELOPER_HREF constant at header.tsx:23 already acknowledges the depth problem by hard-coding a shortcut to the Developer tab, but that shortcut is not a nav item.

Meanwhile Assets, Attack Surface and Public Scans are sub-tabs of History via HistoryViewTabs (components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx:8-13), which is a sensible grouping and shows the pattern already exists.
impact: The two features that create recurring engagement, scheduled scans and webhooks, are the hardest to find, and the one that creates none is the most prominent. A user setting up monitoring has to guess that a scheduling feature lives behind a tab called Developer inside a page called Account Settings.
recommendation: Rebalance without adding nav width. Replace the Badge entry at components/scanner/header.tsx:32 with a Monitoring entry pointing at a new /monitoring route, and give that route the same HistoryViewTabs-style sub-strip holding Scheduled Scans, Webhooks and Alerts. Move SchedulesSection and WebhooksSection there by import, exactly as app/attack-surface/page.tsx:54 already does for DomainsSection, and remove their sub-tab entries from DEVELOPER_SECTIONS (profile-developer-tab.tsx:80-81) so the Developer tab is left with API Keys alone, at which point rename that tab to API. Move Badge to the profile Social tab, next to the other share and embed affordances, which is where a one-time embed snippet belongs.

title: The scanning card is a boxed progress bar over a two-column grid of 20 identical status rows, which is the templated pattern the design language names, and its labels clip on a phone
description:
Measured against audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md and its 14-point checklist. The scanning state is app/dashboard/page.tsx:910-922, a single centred `<div className="flex justify-center pt-10 sm:pt-16">` wrapping components/scanner/scanning-indicator.tsx.

DEVIATIONS, each verified at a line:

1. Tell-tale 5 and E1. scanning-indicator.tsx:307-344 is a `grid grid-cols-1 ... sm:grid-cols-2` of up to 20 rows, every row structurally identical: a 14px `rounded-full` glyph followed by a truncated label. That is the named anti-pattern in list form. The design language's alternatives for exactly this job are the divided list (`divide-y divide-border/50`), the mono-term `<dl>`, and the real table (D4). Four of the nine landing sections use no card grid at all.

2. Tell-tale 4, accent restraint. The doctrine is at most two accented elements per section, documented twice in code comments (landing-categories.tsx:6-11, landing-open-source.tsx:18-19). This card has: the mode pill (:262, `border-primary/20 bg-primary/10 text-primary`), the bar fill (:300, `bg-primary`), and one primary-tinted circle per completed row (:321, `border-primary/40 bg-primary/15 text-primary`) plus the running one (:322, `border-primary bg-primary`). By the last second of a full scan that is roughly 22 primary-tinted elements in one card.

3. Tell-tale 1 and C1. Section rhythm is `py-16 sm:py-20`. The scanning state uses `pt-10 sm:pt-16` with no bottom padding of its own (app/dashboard/page.tsx:911), a third value.

4. C5 radius ladder. `:259` is `rounded-md`, which resolves to `calc(var(--radius) - 2px)` via tailwind.config.mjs:75-79 and is the BUTTON radius. The spec's content card is `rounded-xl`. components/scanner/scan-form.tsx:562 and components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx:182 make the same choice, so all three surfaces of this page are consistent with each other and none matches the spec.

5. C1 divider opacity. "`border-border/50` is the divider, not `border-border`. Full opacity is reserved for the footer's outer edge and card outlines." The internal dividers here are `border-b border-border` (:261) and `border-t border-border` (:307), both full opacity. The house content card (D1) uses `border-b border-border/60` internally.

6. D3 pill idiom. `:262` is `rounded border ... px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium`. The house pill is `rounded-full`, `text-[10px]`, mono or `uppercase tracking-wider`, border at /25 to /30. The severity badge is the one deliberate `rounded` exception and this is not it, so it is a third pill grammar.

7. B2 type scale, and it is also an a11y defect (filed separately as scanui-08): the card has no heading of any kind. `ScanHero` (the page's only `<h1>`) lives inside the `status === "idle"` branch at app/dashboard/page.tsx:887 and is unmounted the instant scanning starts.

8. MOBILE, the one measurable usability defect here. The row label at :331-338 is `min-w-0 truncate` inside a `grid-cols-1` column below the `sm` breakpoint, so it clips on one line with no wrap, no `title` attribute and no tooltip. The strings it clips are the longest ones in FAMILY_STEP: "Parsing page content for mixed content and inline script" (55 chars), "Probing forms & endpoints for XSS, SQLi, SSTI & more" (51), "Looking for leaked paths, versions and stack traces" (50). Derived from the class list rather than measured in a browser: at a 375px viewport the available text width is roughly 375 minus 32 (main `px-4`) minus 32 (card `px-4`) minus about 22 (glyph plus `gap-2`), so about 289px, against roughly 300 to 310px needed for 55 characters at `text-xs`. At 640px and up the same strings sit in a half-width column and clip harder. Also, at one column the list is 20 rows tall, so on a 667px phone the card runs past the fold for a state that lasts a few seconds.

9. Tell-tale 14, motion. globals.css:141-151 collapses CSS `animation-duration` and `transition-duration` under `prefers-reduced-motion`, so the bar's `transition-[width] duration-500` (:300) is covered. The `requestAnimationFrame` settle ramp at :227-248 is not: it writes `style={{ width }}` from JS over SETTLE_ANIMATION_MS and ignores the media query entirely.

10. Structural. The three states are three mutually exclusive full-page branches (app/dashboard/page.tsx:885-958). Submitting the form unmounts ScanHero, ScanForm and the whole Dashboard widget block and replaces them with one small centred card; completion unmounts that card and mounts DashboardResults. Nothing is shared between them, so the page's contents are wholly swapped twice per scan.
impact: This is the highest-traffic transient surface in the product: every scan passes through it, and it is the surface the section brief singles out as reading AI-generated. The mobile clipping is a real loss of information, not a matter of taste: on a phone the user cannot read what is currently running. The three-way content swap means the page never feels like one thing filling in, which is what a scanner should feel like.
recommendation:
Rebuild as one surface that transforms in place. Concretely, so a developer can build it without re-deciding anything. STRUCTURE. Keep the page container `w-full max-w-6xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6` (already `CONTAINER` at app/dashboard/page.tsx:61). Replace the `flex justify-center pt-10 sm:pt-16` wrapper with `py-16 sm:py-20` (C1 standard rhythm) and do not centre: left-align, like every other app surface. HEADING BLOCK, mirroring ScanHero's geometry so the swap from idle is a text change, not a layout change:

Scanning {hostname}

797 checks across 18 families. Findings appear here as each family reports, before the run finishes.

Pull 797 and 18 from lib/config/check-stats.generated.ts (`EXACT_CHECK_COUNT`, `EXACT_CHECK_CATEGORY_COUNT`), never hardcoded (tell-tale 8). BODY, 2-column asymmetric split (E2 idiom, mirrors the hero): `grid gap-8 lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_minmax(0,1.15fr)] lg:gap-12`. LEFT: the run readout, in the ResponseReadout grammar (components/shared/response-readout.tsx:161-216), which is the house signature and already renders "the literal shape of scanning". `overflow-hidden rounded-xl border border-border bg-card font-mono`. - Header, `flex items-baseline gap-2 border-b border-border/60 bg-muted/20 px-5 py-3`: `GET` in `shrink-0 font-semibold text-primary`, then `min-w-0 flex-1 truncate text-foreground` hostname, then the mode label as plain `text-xs text-muted-foreground` (drop the pill entirely; it is the least important thing on screen and it is costing an accent). - Body, `px-5 py-4`: one line of `text-sm text-foreground` carrying the current family's FAMILY_STEP sentence (keep those strings verbatim, they are the best copy in the file), then the bar, then a mono-term `
` (D4 pattern 2): `
` with rows FAMILIES `12 / 18`, CHECKS `531 / 797`, FOUND `7`, values in `font-mono tabular-nums text-foreground`. - Bar: `h-1.5 w-full overflow-hidden rounded-full bg-muted` with a `bg-primary transition-[width] duration-300 ease-out` fill. Reuse the geometry of `SeverityDistribution` (components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:129-190), which is already the canonical "one bar, not five cards" aggregate. - Family list, replacing the 20-cell grid: a `divide-y divide-border/50` list, each row `flex items-baseline justify-between gap-3 py-2`. Left is `CATEGORY_META[c].label` (lib/scanner/category-meta.ts, client-safe, 14 chars at most: "Info disclosure"), right is `font-mono text-xs tabular-nums` check count for that family. State encoded by weight, not by 20 tinted circles: pending `text-muted-foreground/50`, done `text-muted-foreground` with the count in `text-foreground`, running `text-foreground font-medium` on a row carrying `border-l-2 border-primary pl-3`. That single rail is the only accent in the list, which brings the card to three accented elements total (the `GET` word, the bar fill, the one rail). - Footer, `flex items-center justify-between gap-3 border-t border-border/60 bg-muted/20 px-5 py-2.5 text-xs`: cancel on the left as `

title: A shared scan report has no per-report metadata or image: every share link is titled "Shared Scan Report", described with the site-wide app description, and carries the generic marketing OG card
description: app/shared/[token]/layout.tsx:7 is the only metadata source for the route and it calls privatePageMetadata("Shared Scan Report", "/shared"). lib/seo/metadata.ts:130 expands that to pageMetadata with description = APP_DESCRIPTION (the generic site description), image = SEO_OG_IMAGE ("/og-image.png", the static marketing card), and canonical/og:url = APP_URL + "/shared", a path that has no route at all (there is no app/shared/page.tsx). app/host/[hostname]/layout.tsx:8 does the same with "Host Report" and "/host". Nothing per-report reaches the head. There is no opengraph-image.tsx anywhere in the repo and no use of next/og or ImageResponse (grepped across app/, components/, lib/, scripts/): zero dynamic social images exist. The data needed is already available server side by token: app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts:30 selects sh.url, sh.summary, sh.findings_count and sh.scanned_at from scan_history by SHA-256 token hash, with the expiry and revocation gates already written. The page itself cannot supply it (app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:1 is "use client" and fetches in useEffect), but the layout is a server component and can export generateMetadata({ params }). The rendering toolchain also already exists: public/og-image.svg is a 1200x630 template whose right-hand card is literally a mock scan result ("your-domain.com / RISK SCORE 2 of 10 / TOP FINDINGS"), and scripts/build-og-image.mjs rasterizes it with sharp.
impact: The strongest visual asset the project owns (AUDIT-011 names the OG image one of its three best artifacts) is spent showing a fake domain and fake findings, while the real ones are one query away. A share of a genuine report previews identically to a share of the homepage, so nothing in the unfurl tells a reader that someone scanned a specific site and found specific problems. That is the entire viral mechanic of this product category, unused. Note the privacy math is favourable: whoever the unfurler is already holds the token, which grants the full report, so putting the hostname and severity counts in the head leaks nothing the link does not already grant.
recommendation: Add `export async function generateMetadata({ params })` to app/shared/[token]/layout.tsx that hashes the token the same way app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts:24 does, selects url, summary and scanned_at, and returns pageMetadata({ noIndex: true, title: `Security scan of ${hostname}`, description: `${critical} critical, ${high} high and ${medium} medium findings on ${hostname}, scanned ${date} by VulnRadar. Open the full report.`, image: `/shared/${token}/opengraph-image` }). Fall back to the current generic strings when the token misses, is expired, or is revoked, so an invalid link leaks nothing. Then add app/shared/[token]/opengraph-image.tsx using ImageResponse from next/og (bundled with next 15.5.23, no new dependency) at size 1200x630, laid out as the right-hand card of public/og-image.svg: hostname, risk score out of 10, and the top five finding titles with severity dots in the --severity-* colours. Do the same for app/host/[hostname]/. twitter.card is already "summary_large_image" via lib/seo/metadata.ts:116, so nothing else changes.

title: The 749 check pages call generateStaticParams and produce zero prerendered HTML, so the entire organic surface is an uncacheable per-request render and Cloudflare returns a MISS on 100 percent of crawler traffic
description: This is the SEO quantification of AUDIT-012#fe-01 and AUDIT-012#perf-17 (root cause: app/layout.tsx:146 awaits headers() for the CSP nonce, which opts every segment beneath it into per-request dynamic rendering). Do not re-file the root cause. What matters for section 19 is the shape of the loss. app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:34 exports generateStaticParams() returning all 749 check ids, and the file's own comment at lines 29-31 states it produces nothing: "The root layout reads headers() for its CSP nonce, so the whole app already renders per-request." app/checks/category/[category]/page.tsx:27 and app/alternatives/[competitor]/page.tsx:17 do the same. AUDIT-012#fe-01 measured the committed build: .next/prerender-manifest.json lists exactly 5 prerendered routes (robots.txt, sitemap.xml, manifest.webmanifest, llms.txt, llms-full.txt) against 311 app-build-manifest entries, and Next sets `cache-control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate` on dynamically rendered app pages. The sitemap I computed from lib/seo/routes.ts contains 805 URLs: 33 hand-listed, 18 categories, 5 alternatives, 749 checks. Every one is an origin React render with an uncacheable response, on the same single Node process that runs scans. No route sets `revalidate`, so there is no ISR fallback either. On top of that, AUDIT-012#fe-02 measured that the root-layout ChatWidget puts react-markdown plus remark-gfm (144 KB raw / 44 KB gzipped) and an /api/v3/ai/info request on all 311 routes, and AUDIT-011#docs-05 measured /checks at ~190 KB of HTML for 754 list items.
impact: Crawl budget is spent on origin CPU rather than edge bytes: a full Googlebot pass over the sitemap is 805 cold server-side renders, each also serving a JS bundle Googlebot must parse in its rendering pass, with a Cache-Control header that forbids both the CDN and Googlebot's own cache from reusing anything on the next crawl. Nothing in this repo can be measured for TTFB here (no build, no deploy, no Docker on this machine), but the mechanism is unambiguous: the HTML cache hit rate on the organic surface is structurally zero, and content that is byte-identical between deploys is regenerated for every crawler hit and every visitor. Crawler traffic also directly competes with scan execution for the same CPU, so an organic traffic spike degrades the product.
recommendation: Separate the SEO surface from the nonce. Move the public content routes (/checks, /checks/category, /alternatives, /tools, /docs, /legal, /landing, /pricing) into a route group such as app/(marketing)/ with its own layout.tsx that does NOT call headers(), and lift the inline auth-cache script out of the root layout for that group (it is only useful to signed-in users, who are not on these pages). Those routes then prerender from their existing generateStaticParams and become CDN-cacheable. Because the inline script's content is deterministic (it is built from STAFF_ROLES at build time), the alternative fix is a hash-based CSP for that one script, which lets the root layout drop headers() entirely. Either way, add `export const revalidate = 86400` to the check and category routes so a content edit still reaches the edge without a deploy. Verify by checking that .next/prerender-manifest.json lists the 749 check routes after the change.

title: A failed team-members fetch renders "Members 0" over a blank list, "0 members, Your role: " with the role blank, and silently strips every management control from the owner
description: app/teams/page.tsx:280-293 (`refreshMembers`) fetches GET /api/v3/teams/members and only acts inside `if (res.ok)`. On a non-ok response or a thrown request, `members`, `invites` and `currentRole` all keep their prior values (on first open: `[]`, `[]` and `""` from :59), `membersLoading` goes false in the finally at :291, and no error is recorded anywhere. components/teams/team-members-list.tsx then renders the loaded branch: :58-63 prints the header "Members" with the count `members.length`, which is 0, and :182-190 falls to a `divide-y` container with nothing in it, because there is no empty branch at all. The role explainer at :181 is gated on `members.length > 0` so it vanishes too. Separately, `currentRole` staying "" makes `hasTeamPermission("", ...)` false everywhere, so components/teams/team-detail-header.tsx:59-60 hides the rename control and the Invite button, and :132 renders `Your role: ` with an empty span. A team always contains at least its owner, so `members.length === 0` is not a state the data can produce: it is reachable only through a failed fetch, which means the blank card is always a lie.
impact: A team owner opening their own team during a backend blip is told the team has zero members, sees their own role as blank, and finds the Invite and Rename controls gone. The natural reading is that they were removed from their own team or that their permissions were revoked. There is no retry, no message, and nothing distinguishes it from a real permission change. The identical shape applies to `handleViewMemberScans` at :459-479, where a failed fetch renders a member's scan list as empty, which in a compliance context reads as "this person has run no scans".
recommendation: In app/teams/page.tsx:280-293 add an else branch setting the existing `actionError` state, which already has a rendered destructive band at :515-525, with "Couldn't load this team's members. Nothing has changed, try again." and keep the previous members array rather than showing zero. In components/teams/team-members-list.tsx add an explicit branch for `!loading && members.length === 0` that renders an error block rather than a blank div, since that state is unreachable from real data. Do not set `currentRole` from a failed response; leave the header's role chip and its permission-gated controls in a pending state instead of silently resolving to viewer-level.

title: Every PUBLIC_PATHS entry skips the CSRF check entirely, including POST /api/v3/auth/login and the session-authenticated POST /api/v3/badge/site
description: middleware.ts computes `isPublicPath` at line 265 and, when it matches, returns at line 291 -- 25 lines BEFORE the `if (pathname.startsWith("/api/v3/") && !isExemptFromCsrf(pathname))` block at line 316 that calls enforceCsrf(). So the narrow, deliberately-curated exemption list in isExemptFromCsrf (line 350, which AUDIT-010#security-03 tightened from a prefix match to exact paths) is not the real exemption list: PUBLIC_PATHS is, and it is much wider. It exempts POST /api/v3/auth/login, /signup, /forgot-password, /reset-password, /accept-tos, /2fa/verify, /2fa/email-send, /verify-email, /resend-verification (lib/config/public-paths.ts:21-28), the prefixes "/api/v3/auth/discord", "/api/v3/auth/oauth", "/api/v3/badge", "/api/v3/shared", "/api/v3/stripe/setup-webhook", "/api/v3/stripe/setup-products", and "/api/v3/account/unsubscribe". Two concrete consequences. (1) Login CSRF: parseBody (lib/api/api-utils.ts:210-221) falls through to `request.json()` for any content-type that is not multipart/form-data, so a cross-origin `<form enctype="text/plain">` whose single field name is `{"email":"attacker@x","password":"p","z":"` and value is `"}` posts valid JSON to /api/v3/auth/login; the handler at app/api/v3/auth/login/route.ts:274 calls createSession(), whose Set-Cookie the browser stores, and the victim is now signed into the attacker's account. (2) app/api/v3/badge/site/route.ts:14 is a session-cookie-authenticated POST that lives under the "/api/v3/badge" prefix (lib/config/public-paths.ts:154) and reads its body with `req.json()` at line 19 -- the same text/plain form reaches it and mints host_badges rows on a logged-in victim's account.
impact: The login-CSRF instance is the same class of attack as auth-01 and reaches the same outcome (victim silently operating inside the attacker's account) through the password endpoint rather than Discord, so fixing auth-01 alone does not close it. Structurally, the bigger problem is that adding a path to PUBLIC_PATHS -- which reads as 'no login required' -- silently also removes CSRF protection, so any future session-authenticated mutating route added under a public prefix (as /api/v3/badge/site already is) becomes forgeable with no code review signal.
recommendation: In middleware.ts, hoist the CSRF block above the `if (isPublicPath)` return: move lines 316-321 (the `pathname.startsWith("/api/v3/")` + enforceCsrf call) to just after `const hasBearerToken` is computed and before the public-path branch at line 273, so isExemptFromCsrf becomes the single authority on what is exempt. Nothing in PUBLIC_PATHS legitimately needs the exemption -- every same-origin fetch from the app sends an Origin header -- and the three that genuinely do (Stripe webhook, Discord callback, demo-scan) are already listed in isExemptFromCsrf.

title: The host-report trend request cannot start until the host report resolves, because the chart is mounted inside the result-gated subtree
description: app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx is a client component whose entire body is gated on a useEffect fetch. The effect at line 64-85 calls `fetch(API.HOST(hostname))`; the report subtree is rendered only under `{!loading && !error && result && (` at line 179; `<DangerScoreTrend hostname={...} />` is passed as the afterSummary prop at line 277, inside that gate. DangerScoreTrend then runs its own effect (components/host/danger-score-trend.tsx:43-59) calling `fetch(API.HOST_TREND(hostname))`. The two endpoints are independent -- the trend route keys only off the hostname in the URL -- so request B is serialized behind request A for no reason. And because the page is "use client" with no server-side data fetch, the first paint for a visitor or a crawler is the skeleton at line ~150 until ~442 KB gzipped of JS parses and one round trip completes.
impact: Public host reports, which are indexable pages, show a skeleton until JS has downloaded, parsed, and completed a round trip, and then wait for a second serialized round trip before the trend chart can appear. LCP on the route is two sequential network hops plus a large parse, and crawlers that do not execute JS see no report content at all.
recommendation: Fetch the host report on the server. Convert app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx into a server component that awaits the same query the /api/v3/host/[hostname] route runs, issue the host and trend queries with `Promise.all`, and pass both down; keep only the interactive pieces (copy button, issue selection, back button) as client leaves. If a full conversion is too large, at minimum hoist the trend fetch out of DangerScoreTrend into the page's existing effect so both requests start together.

title: /changelog ships the entire 304 KB changelog dataset to the browser (259 KB chunk, 89 KB gzipped) to render four releases
description: components/changelog/changelog-list.tsx is "use client" and imports CHANGELOG from lib/changelog/data at line 7. lib/changelog/data.ts is 304,458 bytes / 4,636 lines of release records. Because the importer is a client component, the whole array is serialized into the route's client chunk: .next/static/chunks/app/changelog/page-73e8592bdfbd7e4b.js is 259 KB raw / 89,359 bytes gzipped, and the route totals 1,067 KB raw / 337 KB gzipped, second only to /host. The component then renders `INITIAL_BATCH = 4` releases (line 13) and reveals four more at a time via an IntersectionObserver sentinel. The page shell around it (app/changelog/page.tsx) is already a server component, so nothing forces the data to the client.
impact: Anyone opening /changelog downloads 89 KB gzipped of release history to see four entries, and the payload grows with every release appended per the project's own changelog-per-change rule. On a phone connection this is several seconds of transfer and parse before the first four entries paint.
recommendation: Keep lib/changelog/data on the server: in app/changelog/page.tsx slice CHANGELOG server-side and pass the first page of releases plus a total count into ChangelogList as props, and serve later batches from a small route handler (or a server action) that the existing IntersectionObserver sentinel calls. Alternatively render the whole list server-side as static HTML and keep only the collapse/expand behaviour client-side.

title: The notification bell and the site-notification banner both GET /api/v3/notifications/active with identical parameters on every page load, then each filter the same payload client-side
description: components/shared/site-notifications.tsx:674-706 (SiteNotificationsWrapper, mounted at app/layout.tsx:188) builds `?authenticated=..&staff=..` and fetches /api/v3/notifications/active, then keeps only type banner/modal/toast. components/shared/notification-center.tsx:290-319 builds the same two params, fetches the same URL, and keeps only type bell -- and re-polls it on setInterval every clientConfig.notificationPollIntervalMs (default CONFIG_NOTIFICATION_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 300000, lib/config/config-values.ts:1097). A second interval at components/shared/notification-center.tsx:344 polls API.NOTIFICATIONS on the same schedule. So every page load issues two identical requests for one payload, and every open tab keeps one of them cycling forever.
impact: Every page view in the app doubles the request count and the database work for site notifications, including anonymous visitors on the public marketing pages (the wrapper runs regardless of sign-in state). The duplication is invisible in normal use, which is exactly why it will not be noticed as traffic grows.
recommendation: Fetch /api/v3/notifications/active once and share it. Move the fetch into a small SWR hook (e.g. lib/hooks/use-active-notifications.ts) keyed on the `authenticated`/`staff` params, have both SiteNotificationsWrapper (components/shared/site-notifications.tsx:687) and NotificationCenter (components/shared/notification-center.tsx:297) consume it, and keep the type filtering where it is. SWR's dedupingInterval then collapses the two calls into one and the existing 5-minute refresh becomes a single revalidation.

title: Client-side render crashes are logged only to the visitor's own browser console, while app/error.tsx tells them "This has been logged"
description: Every error boundary in the app reports into the browser only. app/error.tsx:21-23 is `useEffect(() => { console.error(\`[${APP_NAME}] Unhandled error:\`, error); }, [error])`; app/global-error.tsx:19-21, app/dashboard/error.tsx:24-25, app/admin/error.tsx:14-15, app/history/error.tsx:14-15 and app/profile/error.tsx are all the same one-liner. lib/database/error-log-capture.ts's installErrorLogCapture wraps console.error on the server only, from instrumentation.ts's register() (see its file header at :1-17), so none of those calls ever reach system_error_logs. There is no client-error reporting endpoint anywhere under app/api (no route matching error/telemetry/report other than the admin read-only viewers app/api/v3/admin/error-logs and email-logs). Meanwhile app/error.tsx:58-61 renders the sentence "This has been logged. Try again, or come back once we have looked at it." and the error.digest panel at :63-90 only renders when `error.digest` exists, which for a client-only render error it does not.
impact: The operator has zero visibility into client-side breakage. This project's single most-reported production failure mode is stale-deploy chunk 404s served as text/html (see the deploy-chunk-mismatch history), which manifests exactly as a client-side throw, and none of it is recorded server-side. The user is simultaneously told the error was logged, which is false, and given no reference to quote to support.
recommendation: Add a small rate-limited POST /api/v3/client-errors that accepts `{ message, digest, route }`, console.errors it server-side (which routes it into system_error_logs via the existing wrapper), and call it from app/error.tsx:22 and app/global-error.tsx:20 alongside the existing console.error. Change the copy at app/error.tsx:59 to only claim the error was logged when a digest or a successful report exists.

title: The root layout reads headers() for a CSP nonce, which forces all ~790 public SEO pages to be server-rendered per request with no static or ISR output
category: no static rendering anywhere in the app
description: `RootLayout` does `const nonce = (await headers()).get('x-nonce') ?? undefined` at app/layout.tsx:146. The comment above it (lines 139-145) states the consequence outright: this "forces this layout (and everything under it) into per-request dynamic rendering". app/checks/[id]/page.tsx repeats it at lines 29-31 -- `generateStaticParams` still enumerates the id space (line 34) but the pages are never actually prerendered. `getAllChecks()` returns the full check inventory (lib/seo/checks-content.ts:142), which is the ~754-page /checks tree, plus /checks/category/*, /docs, /finding-types, /host/* and the legal pages -- roughly 790 public routes, every one of which runs the full React server render on every single hit.
impact: Googlebot crawling the /checks tree, or any traffic to the SEO surface the project deliberately built for discovery, costs a full server render per page view with zero cache. The same CPU is shared with the scan engine's synchronous check loop (AUDIT-011 scan-06) in one Node process, so crawler traffic directly slows scans. It also means `next build` produces no static output for content that never changes between deploys.
recommendation: Move the nonce out of the layout's render. Either (a) have middleware.ts inject the nonce into the response HTML stream so the layout stays static, or (b) switch the CSP for the static content routes to a hash-based or `strict-dynamic`-with-no-nonce policy, and drop the `headers()` read from app/layout.tsx so /checks, /docs and the legal pages can be prerendered and revalidated on a long interval. Keep the nonce path for the authenticated app routes that genuinely need per-request rendering.

title: The ToS gate blocks the unsubscribe link in every marketing email
description: components/auth/tos-gate.tsx:9 sets SKIP_TOS_PATHS to ["/login", "/signup", "/legal"]. The logged-out path is fine because :28-31 sets status skip when /api/v3/auth/me is not ok. The exposure is a signed-in user with pending or needs_reaccept status, for whom the page renders at opacity-20 blur-xs pointer-events-none behind TosModal (:77-91). /unsubscribe, /verify-email and /reset-password are not in the skip list.
impact: The unsubscribe link in every marketing email is gated behind accepting updated terms. Coupled with auth-05, the unsubscribe flow is compromised at both ends.
recommendation: Add "/unsubscribe", "/verify-email", "/reset-password" and "/forgot-password" to SKIP_TOS_PATHS.

title: Auth pages prerender a null Suspense fallback, so first paint is empty and the indexable /login is one empty div
description: app/reset-password/page.tsx:41 uses Suspense fallback={null}, prerendered into the static HTML, while the pitch column is hidden lg:block. First paint on a phone is wordmark, empty band, footer. The same shape at app/login/page.tsx:12 and app/signup/page.tsx:12 replaces the entire page.
impact: A blank first paint on the three highest-intent pages in the product, and the HTML a crawler receives for the indexable /login is a single empty div.
recommendation: Give each Suspense a real skeleton fallback.

title: The unsubscribe page prints an email address with no break-all and scrolls the page sideways
description: app/unsubscribe/page.tsx:293 and :324 render redactEmail() output with no break-all, while three sibling components have it.
impact: A long address scrolls the whole page horizontally.
recommendation: Add break-all.

title: The unsubscribe page crushes 19 preference rows into max-w-sm while an unused wide variant exists for exactly this screen
description: app/unsubscribe/page.tsx:393 renders a 19-row preference list inside max-w-sm, leaving about 1050px empty on either side at 1440px. components/auth/auth-layout.tsx:9-11 documents an unused width="wide" prop with a docstring saying it is 'for the one screen that is a list rather than a form', which is this screen.
impact: The page is needlessly cramped, and the fix already exists in the codebase unused.
recommendation: Pass width="wide".

title: The browser session viewer renders raw runtime error strings to the user
description: app/browser/[id]/page.tsx:153-155 sets `e instanceof Error ? e.message : ...` and renders it at :546. A stale-deploy HTML response therefore surfaces `Unexpected token '<', "<!DOCTYPE "... is not valid JSON` to the user. The same shape at :319-323 renders {logsError} raw at :670-672, which can be literally 'HTTP 502'. For contrast components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx:257-275 deliberately shows the scanner's message, and that is safe because app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:288-292 sets details to a fixed string.
impact: Users see JSON parser internals. Given the known stale-deploy chunk-404 failure mode in this project, this is the error they are most likely to hit.
recommendation: Keep the raw text in console.error and render a fixed sentence.

title: The subscription is created before card validation, leaving an orphan incomplete subscription on every typo
description: components/billing/stripe-checkout.tsx:210 creates the Stripe subscription before calling elements.submit(). The other three billing components validate first and carry a comment explaining why.
impact: Every mistyped card leaves an orphan incomplete subscription on the customer record, polluting billing data and potentially triggering dunning.
recommendation: Call elements.submit() first, matching components/billing/ai-credit-checkout.tsx.

title: The checkout success page only understands subscriptions, so credit top-ups warn about a payment that succeeded
description: app/checkout/success/checkout-success-content.tsx:13 is the return_url for all four checkout flows but only polls verify-subscription. A redirect-method credit top-up polls for about 22.5 seconds and then warns the payment could not be confirmed. redirect_status=failed is ignored entirely, so a genuinely failed payment also lands on a page implying success is pending.
impact: A successful purchase is reported as possibly failed, and a failed purchase is reported as probably fine. Both directions are wrong on the money path.
recommendation: Branch on the product type in the return URL and read redirect_status.

title: The support tickets section renders nothing while loading, so /contact looks like the feature is missing
description: components/contact/support-tickets.tsx:174 is `if (isLoading) return null`, under the first and most prominent category on /contact.
impact: On a cold load the page appears not to have a ticket feature at all.
recommendation: Render a skeleton instead of null.

title: /donate removes its own fallback link at the moment it is needed and traps the back button in a redirect loop
description: app/donate/page.tsx:14-22 redirects via window.location.href after 100ms and sets redirected true. At :51-60 the manual 'Continue to Stripe' button renders only when !redirected, and a thank-you message replaces it when redirected. Three defects compound: the fallback disappears exactly when the automatic redirect has failed; location.href rather than location.replace() leaves /donate in history, so Back from Stripe returns here and re-fires after 100ms; and the page has no nav, no <main> and no footer, so a stranded user has no way off it.
impact: A user whose redirect fails is shown a thank-you for a donation that never happened, with no link to complete it and no navigation. Pressing Back from Stripe creates an inescapable loop.
recommendation: Use location.replace(), keep the fallback link rendered unconditionally, drop the premature thank-you, and wrap the page in PublicPageShell.

title: Checkout columns are misaligned between 768px and 1024px by a hardcoded top padding
description: app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:306 uses a magic md:pt-[120px] to align the second column.
impact: The two columns visibly misalign across the whole tablet band on the payment page.
recommendation: Align with a grid row rather than a hardcoded pixel offset.

title: /checks ships roughly 754 list items and 190KB of HTML that never paints
description: app/checks/page.tsx:147-188 renders an <li> for every one of roughly 754 checks across 18 categories, each with a SeverityPill carrying three inline style properties and a Link, all inside collapsed <details> elements.
impact: Slow first paint on a phone, on the page whose entire purpose is to rank in search and be read by mobile arrivals.
recommendation: Inline only the first N categories and link the rest to the existing /checks/category/[category] pages, or move the full index behind a crawlable ?all=1. The 754 individual check pages are intentional SEO surface and stay.

title: The root 404 has no public chrome and its primary button sends logged-out visitors to the dashboard
description: No in-scope content route has its own not-found.tsx, so all three dynamic content routes fall through to the root one, which renders no LandingNav, no Footer, and a primary button linking to ROUTES.DASHBOARD. The same shape applies to app/error.tsx:103.
impact: A logged-out visitor landing on a stale /checks/some-renamed-id from a search result gets a chrome-less 404 whose main button bounces them through middleware to /login. The likeliest visitor to a dead check URL is exactly the person with no account.
recommendation: Add app/checks/not-found.tsx and app/alternatives/not-found.tsx wrapping SeoPageShell, or make the root 404's primary button conditional on auth and default it to ROUTES.LANDING.

title: The public scans table uses fixed pixel columns that crush the hostname at tablet widths
description: components/public-scans/public-scans-table.tsx:7 and components/public-scans/public-scan-row.tsx:22 use grid-cols-[1fr_150px_150px_90px] with gap-4, which is 390px of fixed columns plus 48px of gaps. At the sm breakpoint (640px) the Site column collapses to about 120px so nearly every hostname truncates, while 'Verdict' renders the word 'Clean' inside 150px.
impact: The one column carrying the information is starved while two columns hold whitespace, on a public directory page.
recommendation: Use sm:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_90px_150px_120px], or move the grid to the md breakpoint and keep the stacked layout through tablet.

title: A blurred full-screen AI modal opens the instant results land, so a finished scan reads as still working
description: app/dashboard/page.tsx:690-692 opens AiChoiceModal on completion, a fixed inset-0 backdrop-blur-xs overlay (components/scanner/ai-choice-modal.tsx:36). Results render underneath but the user must click Skip to see them.
impact: Perceived latency on top of real latency. The scan finishes and the user is shown a blur, which is indistinguishable from more waiting.
recommendation: Do not auto-open on completion. Offer the AI summary as an action on the results view instead, so the payoff of the scan is the first thing visible.

title: Five different page shells across the public surface, with /pricing hand-rolled and /donate having none
description: PublicPageShell (components/shared/public-page-shell.tsx:32) swaps `isLoggedIn ? <Header/> : <LandingNav/>` at :58, covering /changelog, /compare, /contact, /security, /host/[hostname], /public-scans, /shared/[token]. DocsShell, LegalShell and SeoPageShell all use LandingNav unconditionally. /pricing is hand-rolled and renders <LandingNav /> twice (app/pricing/page.tsx:71 and :150) despite computing isLoggedIn at :66. /donate has no nav, no <main> and no footer at all. LandingNav is itself auth-aware (components/landing/landing-nav.tsx:104), so the swap is redundant.
impact: A signed-in user clicking Changelog, then Docs, then Changelog watches the header change identity twice. /donate is a page with no way off it.
recommendation: Move /pricing and /donate onto PublicPageShell and pick one convention for the signed-in header across the four public shells. The non-negotiable half is shell-01: the skip-link id should live in one shell rather than being forgotten by three.

title: Any non-OK teams response logs a signed-in user out
description: app/teams/page.tsx:109-113 is `if (!res.ok) { router.push("/login"); return; }` with no status check. Every sibling gates on 401 and 403 specifically (app/history/page.tsx:226, app/assets/page.tsx:74). The same shape exists at app/profile/page.tsx:296.
impact: A transient 500, 503 or 429 bounces a still-authenticated user to the login screen, which reads as a session bug and erodes trust in the auth system.
recommendation: Gate the redirect on 401 and 403 and render an error state otherwise, matching the sibling pages.

title: Three lookup tables paint status with raw Tailwind palette colours instead of the tokens beside them, including one that reimplements the severity scale the product has a single source of truth for
description: design-language.md A2 records that the codebase is genuinely clean of raw Tailwind palette colours; the exceptions it names are components/ui/badge.tsx and the globals.css safelist. Three more exist, all in lookup tables where a token equivalent is already in use one line away. (1) components/badge/badge-types.ts:27-36 returns text-red-500 / text-amber-500 / text-emerald-500 and bg-red-500/10 / bg-amber-500/10 / bg-emerald-500/10 from getSeverityColor and getSeverityBg, a second severity scale beside the single source of truth at components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:37-78; consumed by components/badge/badge-scan-list.tsx:91,96,101,130. That is tell-tale 9 (severity via SEVERITY_TONE) failing. (2) components/teams/teams-types.ts:62-70 mixes vocabularies inside one table: owner and admin use tokens (--warning, primary), manager uses indigo-500 and operator uses orange-500, member and viewer use --muted. (3) components/shared/stat-icon.tsx:13-14 and its duplicate at components/admin/shared/stat-card.tsx:13-14 carry purple-500 and orange-500 among otherwise tokenised tones. Smaller instances: app/admin/page.tsx:1430,1442,1577 and components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:666,915,1039,1051,1997 use amber-500 and emerald-500; components/admin/staff/staff-list.tsx:412 uses purple-500; components/admin/utils.ts:209 uses emerald-500; components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:309,1349 and components/badge/badge-preview.tsx:114 use emerald-500; app/unsubscribe/page.tsx:288 sets an h1 to text-emerald-500. app/globals.css:9 then safelists eleven of these literal classes with @source inline because the role-badge lookup lives outside Tailwind's content globs.
impact: Since the whole product uses exactly three `dark:` overrides (the theme is entirely token-driven), a raw palette colour is a colour that does not participate in theming at all, and every one of these lands in the light-mode contrast band measured in dsn-01: amber-500 on its own tint is 1.79:1 in light mode, emerald-500 is 2.07:1, orange-500 is 2.27:1. Table (1) also means the /badge page rates a scan on a scale that can drift from the real one, which is precisely what severity-badge.tsx's docblock exists to prevent.
recommendation: (1) Delete getSeverityColor and getSeverityBg from components/badge/badge-types.ts and have components/badge/badge-scan-list.tsx call severityTone() from components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx, mapping its safe/caution/unsafe rating onto info/medium/critical. (2) In components/teams/teams-types.ts change manager to `bg-[hsl(var(--chart-4))]/10 text-[hsl(var(--chart-4))] border-[hsl(var(--chart-4))]/20` only if a fifth hue is genuinely needed; better, drop the per-role hue entirely and distinguish roles by the existing ROLE_ICONS plus a neutral badge, keeping the accent for owner alone. (3) After dsn-06 merges the two tone tables, replace purple-500 and orange-500 in the surviving components/shared/stat-icon.tsx with `bg-[hsl(var(--chart-4))]/10 text-[hsl(var(--chart-4))]` and `--chart-3`, which are the tokens for exactly this job. Then the @source inline safelist at app/globals.css:9 can shrink to whatever the role-badge lookup still needs.

title: The pricing table lifts and shadows its highlighted plan, the only hover-lift-and-shadow treatment in the product
description: components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:72 gives the popular plan `border-primary bg-card shadow-lg shadow-primary/10 lg:-translate-y-1.5` while its three siblings get `border-border/50 bg-card/50`. design-language.md D1 records that shadows in this system are near-invisible (shadow-xs on the shadcn Card, `shadow-xs shadow-black/5` on the hero readout) and tell-tale 10 names `hover:shadow-xl hover:-translate-y-1` as the fail case. This is the static version of it: a coloured glow plus a 6px lift, and it is the only elevated-and-offset card in app/ or components/ outside a modal. The card is already differentiated three other ways (a full-opacity primary border against /50 siblings, a full-opacity bg-card against /50, and an absolutely positioned "Most picked" pill at :77), so the shadow and the lift are the fourth and fifth signals for one fact.
impact: Small, but it is on the page whose entire job is to look trustworthy, and the lift is the single most recognisable marketing-template gesture in web design. Anyone who has seen a SaaS pricing page recognises it immediately, which undercuts the honest-and-specific positioning the landing page spends nine sections building.
recommendation: Change components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:72 to `border-primary bg-card`, dropping shadow-lg, shadow-primary/10 and lg:-translate-y-1.5. The border-versus-border/50 and bg-card-versus-bg-card/50 contrast plus the pill at :77 already carry it, and it matches how the landing page marks its one flagship table row (components/landing/landing-categories.tsx, `border-primary/25 bg-primary/5`, no shadow, no offset). If more emphasis is wanted, add `bg-primary/5` to the popular card rather than elevation.

title: The scan-tag input accepts 50 characters and tells the user so, while the server truncates at the admin-configurable MAX_TAG_LENGTH of 30 with no feedback
description: components/history/scan-tags.tsx:15 sets MAX_CLIENT_TAG_LENGTH = 50, used for the maxLength attribute at :165 and for the error copy at :73, `Keep tags under ${MAX_CLIENT_TAG_LENGTH} characters.` The server does not reject an overlong tag: app/api/v3/scan/tags/route.ts:70-:71 reads getSetting('MAX_TAG_LENGTH') and silently truncates with `tag.trim().toLowerCase().slice(0, maxTagLength)`. The default is 30 (lib/config/config-values.ts:1039, admin-editable at lib/config/registry.ts:2705). The component's own doc comment at :8-:14 acknowledges the split, explaining that 50 is the VARCHAR(50) column guard rather than the enforced limit, so the divergence is deliberate; the message shown to the user is not.
impact: A tag between 31 and 50 characters is accepted by the form, sent, silently shortened, and comes back as a different string than the user typed, with the error copy having just promised them 50 characters were fine. On a deployment that lowered MAX_TAG_LENGTH further, the gap widens with no UI change.
recommendation: Expose MAX_TAG_LENGTH through the existing client config endpoint (app/api/v3/config/client/route.ts already carries FEATURE_PDF_REPORTS), use it for both maxLength and the error copy, and keep 50 only as the hard column guard it is documented to be.

title: "Get Started" is the primary CTA label in the nav and on three pricing surfaces, and it is the one string on the marketing surface that says nothing
description: components/landing/landing-nav.tsx:124 labels the logged-out primary nav button "Get Started". The same string appears at app/pricing/page.tsx:93 (the billing-disabled page's only CTA) and components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:170 (the logged-out paid-plan CTA). It is title case where the rest of the page is sentence case, it names no action, and it is the exact label a generated landing page would use. audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md section F2.4 already records it as the weakest string on the page; this extends that with the two pricing occurrences and with what to put there instead. The full logged-out CTA map above the fold today is: nav "Get Started" to /signup, hero primary "Start scanning free" to /signup, hero secondary "Try the demo" to /demo. Two of three lead to a signup form, and the third leads to a demo that cannot scan the visitor's site (mkt-01). Every other CTA on the page is written properly: "Create a free account", "Try the demo first", "See a full report", "Try it in the playground", "Read the API docs", "Paste a URL and see what comes back".
impact: Minor on its own, but it is the first button a visitor sees and it is inconsistent with a page whose entire argument is specificity. On the billing-disabled self-host page it is also the only CTA, so the whole page ends on the most generic string available.
recommendation: If mkt-01 ships, make the logged-out nav CTA "Scan a URL" pointing at ROUTES.DEMO and leave the ghost "Log in" beside it, so the fastest action is the one in the nav. If it does not, use "Start free" at components/landing/landing-nav.tsx:124. At app/pricing/page.tsx:93 use "Create an account" for the logged-out case, since that page's whole point is that there is nothing to pay for. At components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:170 use "Start free, upgrade later", which is accurate: the button goes to /signup rather than to checkout.

title: The compare run fails silently, leaving the picker on screen with no explanation when a diff is rejected
description: runCompare (app/compare/page.tsx:54-65) sets loading, fetches the compare endpoint with a and b, and does `if (res.ok) setDiffResult(data)` with no else, plus `catch { /* ignore */ }` at :61-63. setLoading(false) then runs at :64 either way. The same function is the deep-link handler at :79, so a stale or invalid ?a=&b= pair in a bookmarked URL takes the same path.
impact: Pressing Compare on two scans the server refuses to diff (different hosts, a scan deleted since the list loaded, a permissions failure) stops the spinner and returns the user to the same picker with both scans still selected and no message, so the only available conclusion is that the button is broken. A shared /compare?a=..&b=.. link whose scans have aged out of retention behaves identically.
recommendation: Add an error state to app/compare/page.tsx, set it from data.error in an !res.ok branch and from the catch, and render it above the Compare button at :275-292 using the same destructive-tinted box the rest of the app uses. For the deep-link path at :78-82, distinguish "these two scans cannot be compared" from "one of these scans no longer exists" and offer handleReset (:200) as the recovery action.

title: The teams member list has no search, sort or pagination and the selected team is not addressable by URL, so Back leaves the page entirely
description: app/teams/page.tsx imports nothing from lib/ui/url-state, so no state on the page reaches the URL: selectedTeam (:56), searchQuery (:49), viewingMember (:89) and scanPage (:95) are all useState. Opening a team is openTeam (:296) mutating state in place with no history entry, so browser Back navigates off /teams entirely rather than returning to the team list, and a team cannot be linked or bookmarked. The member list rendered at :588-603 has no search, no role filter, no sort and no pagination, and pending invites are interleaved with members with no way to isolate them.
impact: Sharing "the acme team page" with a colleague is impossible; the only shareable thing is /teams. Back behaving as leave-the-page is the kind of small wrongness users learn to work around by never using Back on that page. The member list is fine at five seats and unusable at fifty, which is the size at which a team feature starts to matter commercially.
recommendation: Back selectedTeam with useQueryParam("team", "") from lib/ui/url-state.ts:170, the same hook app/repos/page.tsx:134 uses for ?repo, resolving the team from the loaded list on mount so a deep link works, and do the same for viewingMember. Add a name and email search plus a role filter above the member list, both URL-backed per qolf-10, and reuse the existing PaginationControl past roughly 20 members. Separately: there is no member role-change mutation in the UI at all, roles are set only at invite time (:70-72), so an owner who invites someone as a viewer must remove and re-invite them to promote them.

title: Every one of the 805 sitemap URLs carries the same lastmod, the build timestamp, so the field is noise on a 749-page set whose source data changes a few entries at a time
description: app/sitemap.ts:13 computes `const lastModified = new Date()` once and assigns it to every entry at line 17. The comment at lines 10-12 explains the choice as avoiding per-entry timestamp noise, which is right about not calling new Date() per row but produces the opposite of the intended effect: because the route is `force-static` (line 7), the value is frozen at build time and every deploy republishes all 805 URLs with a brand-new identical lastmod. Google's documented position is that it uses lastmod only when it is consistently accurate, and that a site claiming every page changed at the same instant is a signal to ignore the field site-wide. The real modification data exists: the 749 check entries come from lib/scanner/checks-data/*.json (file mtime or git log), the 5 alternatives from lib/seo/alternatives.ts, and the docs pages from their own source files.
impact: The sitemap gives Google no usable freshness signal for 805 URLs, so recrawl scheduling falls back to Google's own heuristics, and the one check page that actually changed after a release is refreshed no sooner than the 748 that did not. On a deploy-frequent repo (3.7.2 with a per-change changelog policy) this republishes the entire sitemap as "all changed" several times a week.
recommendation: Derive lastmod from source. Simplest accurate version: in scripts/compile-checks-knowledge.mjs, which already runs on every prebuild, emit a `{ checkId: isoDate }` map from `git log -1 --format=%cI -- <file>` per checks-data JSON file into lib/config/check-stats.generated.ts, and have CHECK_ROUTES in lib/seo/routes.ts:80 carry a per-route lastModified read from it. Do the same for the docs routes once seo-05 derives them from DOCS_PAGES, using each layout.tsx's git commit date. Keep a single build-time fallback for routes with no source mapping.

title: The indexed check count disagrees across two adjacent marketing surfaces: the landing meta description says "795+ deterministic checks" while the /checks meta description says "the full list of 749 security checks"
description: lib/config/check-stats.generated.ts:8 sets GENERATED_CHECKS_LABEL to "795+", derived from EXACT_CHECK_COUNT = 797 (line 6), which is EXACT_LEGACY_CHECK_COUNT 754 plus EXACT_PAGE_CHECK_COUNT 43. app/landing/page.tsx:32 uses that label verbatim in the landing meta description: "795+ deterministic checks across headers, TLS, cookies, DNS, and secrets". app/checks/page.tsx:26 computes `TOTAL = getAllChecks().length`, which is 754 minus the 5 entries filtered as "(disabled duplicate)" at lib/seo/checks-content.ts:129, giving 749, and line 29 puts that in the /checks meta description: "The full list of 749 security checks VulnRadar runs against a URL". Both numbers are internally defensible (795 counts the 43 PageCheck-architecture detectors that deliberately have no public page, per the comment at lib/seo/checks-content.ts:12-14) and neither is a lie, but they appear in two indexed snippets one click apart and differ by 46.
impact: A visitor who clicks a result promising 795+ checks lands on a page whose own first sentence says 749, which reads as a marketing exaggeration caught in the act. On a product whose entire pitch is deterministic, auditable detection, an unexplained number mismatch on the two highest-traffic public pages is a credibility cost out of proportion to the size of the bug.
recommendation: Make /checks state both numbers so they reconcile rather than contradict. Change app/checks/page.tsx:29 to something like `The ${TOTAL} security checks with a public fix guide, out of ${TOTAL_CHECKS_LABEL} VulnRadar runs, grouped into 18 categories.` and add one sentence to the page body explaining that the remaining detectors run inside multi-page analysis and have no standalone page. Update the first FAQ answer at app/checks/page.tsx:43, which currently says "documents 749 checks", to the same framing so the FAQPage structured data matches.

title: The homepage URL never serves content: / issues a temporary 307 to /landing for anonymous visitors, and the root layout's fallback canonical points at that same redirecting URL
description: middleware.ts:284-289 redirects an anonymous request for "/" to ROUTES.LANDING with NextResponse.redirect(), which defaults to HTTP 307 (temporary). app/page.tsx:7 does the same with redirect("/landing") for anything that reaches it. So the root URL, the one that gets typed, linked and shared, never returns a 200. Meanwhile app/landing/page.tsx:29 sets canonical /landing and lib/seo/routes.ts:26 puts /landing in the sitemap at priority 1.0, so /landing is the declared homepage. Pulling the other way, app/layout.tsx:59 declares `alternates: { canonical: "/" }` as the site-wide fallback, with the comment "Pages without their own canonical fall back to the site root rather than competing with each other": that fallback names a URL that always redirects. It is latent today because all 71 pages set their own canonical (see seo-22), so nothing currently inherits it, but the next page added without a pageMetadata call will canonicalise to a redirect.
impact: Branded results show vulnradar.dev/landing rather than vulnradar.dev, which reads as less authoritative for the site's own name. A temporary redirect also tells Google the arrangement may change, so it keeps evaluating both URLs instead of consolidating cleanly, and every cold homepage visit pays an extra round trip before the first byte of content. Small in absolute terms, but it applies to the single highest-authority URL on the domain.
recommendation: Serve the landing content at / instead of redirecting to it. In middleware.ts:284-289, replace NextResponse.redirect with NextResponse.rewrite(new URL(ROUTES.LANDING, request.url)) for the anonymous root case, so / returns 200 with the landing HTML; the signed-in branch keeps redirecting to /dashboard. Then set the landing canonical to "/" in app/landing/page.tsx:29 and change the sitemap entry at lib/seo/routes.ts:26 from "/landing" to "/", and 301 /landing to / so the old URL consolidates. If the redirect is kept instead, at minimum change it to a 308 (`NextResponse.redirect(url, 308)`) so it is declared permanent, and change the root layout fallback at app/layout.tsx:59 to "/landing" so it names a URL that actually renders.

title: Adding or removing a scan tag no-ops on failure in both the history and dashboard copies: no error, no revert, no indication the click was received
description: app/history/page.tsx:305-319 (`handleAddTag`) and :321-331 (`handleRemoveTag`) POST to API.SCAN_TAGS and do all their work inside `if (res.ok)`. There is no else, no catch at all (an unhandled rejection on a dropped connection), and no error state. app/dashboard/page.tsx:389-400 and :402-412 are the same two functions copied verbatim with the same omission. The tag input at components/history/scan-tags.tsx clears on submit regardless, so the typed tag disappears and never appears in the list. Removing a tag on a failed request leaves the chip in place with no explanation. These are the two handlers AUDIT-011#form-01 did not cover on this page (it named handleSaveNotes at :389 in the pre-refactor numbering).
impact: Tagging is how a user organises scan history, and the failure is completely invisible: the input clears exactly as it does on success, so the user believes the tag was applied and only discovers otherwise when they filter by it later and get nothing. The missing catch also means a network drop produces an unhandled promise rejection rather than any handled path.
recommendation: Wrap all four handlers in try/catch and surface a failure. The history page already has a rendered error slot pattern in its clear-history dialog (`clearError` at :667-669); add an equivalent transient line under the tag row, or reuse the toast used elsewhere on the page. At minimum, do not clear the input in components/history/scan-tags.tsx until the parent's promise resolves, so a failed add leaves the user's text where they can retry it.

title: app/actions/stripe.ts, the 220-statement checkout and credit-purchase server-action surface, is at 56.36% statements and 53.79% branches
description: Measured: app/actions/stripe.ts is 56.36% statements, 53.79% branches, 53.33% functions over 220 statements, the largest under-60% file in the billing area. It imports from lib/billing/browserbase-usage (line 21) and is the entry point users hit to start a checkout and to buy AI, GitHub-review, and Browserbase credit packs. The lower-level catalogs and usage modules around it are all at or near 100% (catalog.ts 100%, ai-credit-catalog.ts 100%, browserbase-credit-catalog.ts 100%, github-credit-catalog.ts 100%, stripe-catalog.ts 100%, plan-limits.ts 100%), so as with the updater in cov-06 the pattern is well-tested primitives with an untested orchestrator. Nearly half the branches are the error, already-subscribed, wrong-plan, and mismatched-currency arms that decide what the user is actually charged for.
impact: Roughly half the decision points on the path that creates a Stripe checkout session are unexercised. A regression in a branch that picks the price id or the quantity charges the wrong amount, and the failure is only visible once a customer complains or the operator reconciles Stripe by hand.
recommendation: Add tests/app/actions/stripe.test.ts with the Stripe SDK mocked, asserting one case per branch that selects a price or quantity: each credit pack maps to its catalog price id, a user already on the target plan is rejected rather than double-charged, an unknown pack id is rejected, and a Stripe API error surfaces as a handled error rather than a thrown server action.

title: The docs component library exports a purpose-built ParamTable and DocsStepCard that no docs page renders, while the API reference renders its parameters with inline markup instead
description: components/docs/index.ts wildcard-exports fourteen modules. Two exported components have no consumer: ParamTable at components/docs/docs-table.tsx:91-164 (74 lines including its doc comment) and DocsStepCard at components/docs/docs-steps.tsx:47-79 (33 lines including its props interface). Neither identifier occurs anywhere in the repo outside its own declaration.
