title: The AI chat widget keeps private copies of the four renderers that components/ai-chat/message-content.tsx was created to own, so the file whose own comment asks to be kept in sync is not the one the live widget uses
description:
components/ai-chat/message-content.tsx exists to be the shared renderer. Its header at :10-18 says so: "The exact react-markdown component overrides the live chat widget (components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx) uses. Kept here ... so any renderer of a stored AI message produces identical output to the widget ... If chat-widget.tsx's copy of these ever changes, this is the one to keep in sync with it (or, better, the one it should import from)." MessageContent's own doc at :123-131 goes further: "This is the single rendering path meant to be shared by the live chat widget and the admin AI-chat viewer, so the two can never drift into two different-looking renderers."

chat-widget.tsx does not import any of it. It defines its own `mdComponents` at :202-283 (byte-identical to messageMarkdownComponents at message-content.tsx:19-96), its own `MarkdownContent` at :283-289, its own `ThinkBlock` at :317-329 (byte-identical to message-content.tsx:111-123), and its own segment renderer at :431-470 that calls parseSegments exactly as MessageContent does at :141-159. Both files independently `import ReactMarkdown from "react-markdown"` and `remarkGfm` (chat-widget.tsx:24-25, message-content.tsx:4-5).

The only consumer of message-content.tsx is app/admin/ai-chats/[id]/page.tsx:9. So the module that documents itself as the shared path is used by one admin page, and the widget it was extracted from still runs the copy.
impact: The bodies are identical today, so nothing is currently wrong on screen. The cost is that the module's stated guarantee is false: a styling or safety change to the chat renderer (a link rel, a code-block escape, the think-tag parser) lands on one of the two and the admin viewer and the live widget diverge, which is precisely what the comment says cannot happen. It is also roughly 130 duplicated lines and a duplicated react-markdown + remark-gfm import graph in the widget that AUDIT-012#fe-02 already flags as 144 KB raw on every page.
recommendation: Delete mdComponents, MarkdownContent and ThinkBlock from components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:202-329 and import messageMarkdownComponents, MarkdownContent and ThinkBlock from @/components/ai-chat/message-content. The widget's :431-470 renderer differs from MessageContent only in that it renders `displayContent` (the typewriter buffer) rather than `content`, so give MessageContent an optional `content` override and use it there too, then delete the fourth copy.

title: The crawl page picker is the best-built selection UI in the product and should be kept as is
description: components/scanner/crawl-url-selector.tsx (283 lines), rendered from app/dashboard/page.tsx:963-970. Persistent footer toolbar with 'N of M selected (max L)', a search filter, and Select all / Clear all. Pre-selects up to the plan cap at :55-64; over-cap rows are disabled at 40% opacity with an explanatory banner. useModalA11y provides focus trap, Escape and focus restore. Mobile works at 320px via max-h-[80vh] with a min-h-0 flex-1 scroll list and text-base sm:text-xs to stop iOS zoom. The backend is a real bulk endpoint: one request carries the whole array and app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:235-272 re-validates and re-enforces the plan cap server-side.
impact: None. Recorded so it is not swept up in a bulk-action removal pass: deleting it does not remove clutter, it removes the crawl feature or forces every crawl to scan every discovered page at the user's expense.
recommendation: Keep. Two optional nits: the rows are buttons with aria-pressed and a fake check glyph rather than real checkboxes, so assistive tech does not announce them as checkboxes; and defaulting to everything pre-selected means a user who wants three pages must deselect the rest.

title: Position on the 2026 agentic-pentest shift: VulnRadar should deliberately not compete, and should use its determinism as the counter-position
description: Every major vendor launched an agentic AI pentest product this year: Invicti Agentic Pentest (announced 29 to 30 July 2026, parallel specialised agents for SQLi, RCE, XSS, SSRF, XXE, insecure deserialization, path traversal and NoSQLi, max $500 per pentest, 24-hour turnaround), Intruder AI Pentesting from $3,500 per test, Astra autonomous agents, and Snyk Evo Continuous Offensive Security. All are aimed at the buyer who needs a pentest report for an auditor, and all are priced 10x to 100x below a human pentest (audits/AUDIT-014/research-competitors-commercial.md, "The 2026 industry shift"). Three facts from this codebase determine the right answer. First, the product's headline promise is the opposite claim: components/landing/landing-features.tsx:26 to :32 is titled "Run it twice, get the same answer twice" and states "There is no model in the detection path deciding today that something is medium when yesterday it was low", which is what makes lib/scanner/regression-alert.ts's diff and the CI gate in .github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml meaningful at all. Second, an agentic pentest requires unattended exploitation against a live target, which this product has structurally refused: the nine active probes are opt-in and gated behind verified domain ownership (lib/scanner/active-probe-catalog.ts:117), and there is no out-of-band channel (comp-11). Third, AI is already used here on the correct side of that line, for triage rather than detection: lib/ai/verify-findings.ts attaches aiVerdict and aiConfidence that re-weight the safety rating (lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts:27 to :40) without changing what the deterministic engine found.
impact: Entering this market would cost the product the one claim it currently wins on, and it would compete on turnaround and exploitation depth against vendors with dedicated infrastructure, insurance and legal cover. Ignoring it silently is also a cost: "why not just buy a $500 agentic pentest" is now a live objection at every price point above free, and there is no answer to it on the site.
recommendation: Do not compete on agentic pentesting. Take the counter-position explicitly, because determinism is a differentiator only if someone states what it is against. Add an FAQ entry to app/landing/page.tsx's buildFaq array, in the existing blunt voice, along these lines: "Do you do AI pentesting? No. The detection engine is deterministic: the same URL produces the same finding IDs every run, which is what lets you fail a build on a specific ID and diff Tuesday against Friday. We use a model to triage and explain findings, never to decide whether one exists." Keep the AI confined to lib/ai/verify-findings.ts's triage role and to the assistant, and never let a model reach the detection path. If a pentest-report artifact is ever wanted, build the attestation page described in comp-14, which is the deliverable that buyer actually needs, rather than the exploitation engine.

title: Negative result: the theme system, motion policy, focus policy and copy discipline are genuinely sound, and the auth flow and the scan result view are the internal reference examples to copy
description: Recorded so a future audit does not redo this. (a) Theming is real, not aspirational: across all of app/ and components/ there are exactly three `dark:` class overrides (components/landing/landing-hero.tsx, components/profile/tabs/developer/schedules-section.tsx, and the shadow on the hero readout). Everything else switches via the CSS variables, which is why dsn-01's contrast fix can be made in one place. (b) Motion: app/globals.css:141-152 sets a global prefers-reduced-motion block that caps animation-duration and iteration-count, so tell-tale 14 passes product-wide even where a component uses animate-pulse. (c) Focus: app/globals.css:370-372 sets a global :focus-visible ring with a documented exclusion for Radix collection items, so tell-tale 13's focus half holds even on the elements that do not opt in locally. (d) Copy: the only em dashes in app/ and components/ are inside code comments and one empty-cell placeholder at components/admin/features/content-manager.tsx:451, so the CLAUDE.md ban is genuinely honoured; "Everything you need" survives only as mid-sentence prose at app/docs/architecture/page.tsx:77 (already AUDIT-011#design F2). (e) The auth flow is the strongest in-app work and should be the model: components/auth/auth-split-layout.tsx:77-146 is a one-canvas asymmetric layout with a real ResponseReadout, a hard-broken two-line headline and a border-l definition list, and components/auth/auth-shell.tsx:22-90 centralises the field class, focus ring, step indicator and heading so every screen in the flow is identical by construction. (f) The scan result view is the strongest data surface: components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx is a genuine single source of truth, SeverityDistribution at :129-190 is one bar with a legend rather than five stat cards exactly as its docblock claims, and components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx carries zero raw palette colours across 300-odd lines. (g) The joined stat strip idiom (`grid grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-4 gap-px bg-border`) is the correct anti-pattern-avoidant shape and is used consistently on /dashboard, /history, /assets and /shares; only its implementation is duplicated (dsn-06), not its design.
impact: None. This is a record of what was checked and found correct.
recommendation: No action. When building a new in-app flow, copy components/auth/auth-shell.tsx's shape: put the shared field class, focus ring and heading component in one module per flow so the screens cannot drift. When building a new data panel, copy components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx. Point new contributors at those two files rather than at the landing page, which is a marketing surface and does not answer in-app questions.

title: Negative results: the nine landing sections, the demo copy and the pricing hero already meet the voice standard, so a future audit should not re-review them
description: Read line by line against the CLAUDE.md voice rules and audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md section F. Zero adjective-only benefit claims of the Lightning Fast / Deep Analysis / Developer First class. title: Verified correct on the scanning page, recorded so the next audit does not re-derive it
description:
Things I checked on this surface and found sound, so they need no work.

1. The progress denominator is genuinely real, not estimated. app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:332-339 derives `categoriesTotal` from `getPlannedSyncCategories` plus `getPlannedAsyncBranches` against the actual selected scanners, and explicitly zeroes the sync side for raw-IP targets to match executeScan's own gating. lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:117-139 persists only events the engine actually emits. Tell-tale 8 (numbers real, not hardcoded) passes on the counter, even though the bar around it does not.

2. The component's ratchet is not a stall. `MIN_STEP_DISPLAY_MS` paces the display only; the parent's `status` flip unmounts the indicator immediately on completion regardless of where the ratchet has got to. The docblock at :46-57 says so and the code matches. No artificial minimum display time exists, confirming AUDIT-011#scan-05's own negative finding still holds.

3. Colour discipline is clean. No `bg-gray-*`, `text-slate-*`, `bg-[#hex]` or raw brand constant appears in scanning-indicator.tsx, dashboard-error-state.tsx or the scanning branch of app/dashboard/page.tsx. Severity in the error card goes through `hsl(var(--severity-medium))` and `bg-destructive` (dashboard-error-state.tsx:98, 106, 216), which is the correct encoding. Tell-tale 3 passes.

4. No em dashes in any user-facing string on this page. Every `--` in these files is inside a code comment.

5. Focus rings are present on both interactive controls: the cancel button (scanning-indicator.tsx:352) and the copy button plus support link in the error card (dashboard-error-state.tsx:241, 294) all carry `focus-visible:outline-hidden focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring`. No `onClick` on a bare div anywhere on this surface. Tell-tale 13 passes on focus, fails only on semantics (scanui-08).

6. `app/dashboard/` has both `loading.tsx` and `error.tsx`, so it is not part of AUDIT-011#drift-13's missing-boundary set.

7. The per-family copy in `FAMILY_STEP` (scanning-indicator.tsx:16-36) is good, specific, mechanism-first writing that matches the voice rules: "Grepping responses for keys and tokens", "Negotiating TLS versions and ciphers", "Looking for leaked paths, versions and stack traces". The rebuild should keep these strings; the problem is the container, not the words. The only nit is the two ampersands at :35.
impact: None. Recorded so a future audit of this surface starts from the open items rather than re-deriving the settled ones.
recommendation: No action. When scanui-03 is built, carry points 3, 4, 5 and 7 forward rather than rewriting them.

title: AI crawler access is blocked by Cloudflare's Managed robots.txt at the edge, not by app/robots.ts, so this is a dashboard toggle and no code change will fix it
description: Recording this so nobody spends a day on the wrong file. app/robots.ts:19-43 already declares an explicit AI_CRAWLERS group naming GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, anthropic-ai, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Google-Extended, Googlebot, Applebot-Extended, CCBot, cohere-ai, Bytespider, Amazonbot and Meta-ExternalAgent, and grants them `Allow: /` with only the same private paths everyone else is denied. The application code is correct and needs no change. Cloudflare's Managed robots.txt (AI Crawl Control) overrides the origin's robots.txt at the edge and Disallows GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot and Google-Extended, which is the confirmed reason AI assistants do not know this product. That is a Cloudflare dashboard setting on the zone, not anything reachable from this repo.
impact: The product publishes /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt and 749 per-check remediation guides specifically so answer engines can cite them, and the edge blocks the crawlers that would read them. Fixing the app's robots.txt would change nothing, because the origin file never reaches those crawlers.
recommendation: The owner toggles Managed robots.txt / AI Crawl Control off in the Cloudflare dashboard for the zone. Verify afterwards by fetching https://vulnradar.dev/robots.txt with `User-Agent: GPTBot` and confirming the response matches what app/robots.ts generates. Do not modify app/robots.ts for this.

title: Positive result: DashboardErrorState, the results-list filtered-empty block, /public-scans, /demo, /browser/[id] and repo-detail are the correct in-repo models for these states and should be reused rather than reinvented
description: Recorded so the fixes above have something concrete to copy and so the next audit does not re-derive it. components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx:43-76 classifies a scan failure into seven kinds (blocked, network, rate_limit, validation, server, auth_failed, generic) from the message and status, and :78-onward gives each one a title, an icon, a severity-toned rail and a description that states what happened and then what to do about it, plus a retry. It is the best error component in the product and the only one that distinguishes retryable from permanent. components/scanner/results-list.tsx:597-621 is the model empty state: it says why the list is empty ("N findings are hidden"), what to do, and offers a one-click Reset filters. app/public-scans/page.tsx:134-145 is the model three-way ladder (skeleton, then error, then empty, then data) in a single page. components/repos/repo-detail.tsx:242-255 is the model four-way ladder, spoiled only by the missing finally described in state-04. app/demo/page.tsx:68-92 and app/browser/[id]/page.tsx:519-546 both carry designed error branches. app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:139-158 is the model "this thing does not exist" state, with a specific explanation and a conversion CTA rather than a bare 404. All of them use the established design language: dashed border-border on bg-card/50 for empty, destructive or severity tones for error, and no shadow beyond the shadow-xs baseline.
impact: None. This is coverage of what is already right, so remediation does not invent a seventh visual grammar for an error block.
recommendation: When fixing state-05, state-07, state-10, state-11 and state-16, reuse these: the classified-kind approach from dashboard-error-state.tsx for anything that needs to distinguish retryable from permanent, the dashed empty block (`rounded-md border border-dashed border-border bg-card/50 px-4 py-12 text-center`) with a title, a why line and an action for anything genuinely empty, and a destructive-toned inline band for a load failure inside an otherwise working page. Do not introduce a new shell.

title: A full Radix toast stack is mounted on every page for exactly one consumer while 50 components hand-roll their own error and success banner state
category: two mechanisms for the same job
description:
components/ui/use-toast.ts (191 lines), components/ui/toast.tsx and components/ui/toaster.tsx implement a Radix-backed toast queue, and app/layout.tsx:195 mounts <Toaster /> inside the root layout so it renders on every route. components/ui/toaster.tsx:13-18 records that this mounting was itself a fix: "Mounted once in app/layout.tsx: without it the toast state updated but nothing ever drew it, so every toast() call (e.g. the billing-verification modal's error/success feedback) was silent."

That billing-verification modal is still the only consumer. components/profile/modals/billing-verification-modal.tsx:138 is the single `useToast()` call site outside components/ui/ itself; it fires nine toasts. Every other surface in the app reports success and failure one of two other ways: a locally held `useState<string | null>(null)` banner pair (50 files) or a setError/setSuccess pair prop-drilled down from the page (the profile tab tree, typed at components/profile/types.ts and threaded through profile-social-tab.tsx, profile-notifications-tab.tsx and developer/domains-section.tsx). A third mechanism, the admin-authored site notification with `type: "toast"`, is rendered by components/shared/site-notifications.tsx and shares nothing with the Radix stack.
impact: No user-visible bug: the modal's toasts work and the banners work. The cost is that feedback looks and behaves differently depending on which of three mechanisms a screen happened to use, that a Radix provider and its dependency ship on every page load for one modal, and that a new contributor picking a pattern has no signal about which one is intended. This is the reason a fix like "errors should auto-dismiss" or "errors should be announced to screen readers" cannot be made once.
recommendation: Decide which one wins and write it in CLAUDE.md. If toasts win, migrate the 50 local-banner components in batches and delete the prop-drilled setError/setSuccess from components/profile/types.ts. If banners win, delete components/ui/toaster.tsx, components/ui/toast.tsx and components/ui/use-toast.ts, drop <Toaster /> from app/layout.tsx:195, and convert components/profile/modals/billing-verification-modal.tsx's nine calls to the banner pattern its parent already uses. Either way this is not urgent; it is worth deciding before the next batch of forms is written.
